aPlusContent.title: Product description
aPlusContent.rawText:
Product description
Montessori Mobile Designed for Baby’s Eye View 
No more boring bottoms! Your baby can now see the full patterns of crib toys hanging, keeping them engaged and visually stimulated. 
Montessori-Inspired for Holistic Development 
Designed to support early development with high contrast - black and white patterns that capture your baby’s attention and stimulate their senses. 
Did You Know? Babies Only See High-Contrast Colors 
They Ignore The Colorful Crib Mobile You Bought! 
That’s why they don’t enjoy bright, low-contrast colors – their vision isn’t fully developed yet. 
Babies Prefer High-Contrast Colors 
High-contrast designs are proven to attract babies more, which is why they love Tinitigies mobiles so much! 
The TINITIGIES music box features 12 soothing lullabies 

The TINITIGIES music box features 12 soothing lullabies, including classics like Twinkle Twinkle Little Star, Brahms’ Lullaby, and Rock-a-Bye Baby. Each melody lasts 1-2 minutes, creating a peaceful atmosphere to calm and stabilize your baby’s sleep. Let’s try putting on the headphones and listen to the melodies of a few songs from the playlist. 
The video showcases the product in use.The video guides you through product setup.The video compares multiple products.The video shows the product being unpacked.
Tinitigies Piano Lullabies
Preset to Lowest Volume for Baby's Comfort 
The music box is preset to the lowest volume level by default to avoid startling your baby when it starts. 
Easy to adjust the volume by holding the button (+) (-) 
Will this crib mobile fit a bassinet? 
This mobile is designed for cribs, not bassinets. Many returns happen because buyers expect it to fit a bassinet, but most bassinet rails are not compatible. Please check the mounting dimensions in our listing images carefully before ordering. 
Why can’t I hear the music when I turn it on? 
The music starts at the lowest volume by design to avoid startling your baby. If you hear little or no sound, simply turn up the volume and make sure the music box is not set to rotation-only mode. 
What modes does the digital music box have? 
It has 3 modes: rotation only, music only, or music + rotation. It also features a 30-minute auto shut-off for bedtime. Requires 2 AA batteries (not included). 
What if the music mechanism stops working within the first year? 
We carefully inspect every music mechanism before shipping. If the mechanism stops working under normal use within 1 year, we will replace it one-for-one at no charge.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: A great phone...but compared to what?
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Tldr: Good phone for this price, noticeably better than older A13 and I wish more people would include context to their reviews. Glad I bought mine.I'm leaving a long and detailed review because I got tired of reading through reviews that seemed contradictory, or said something was "bad" but without any context. If I made a poor choice buying a phone I'd likely be stuck with it for some years. I'm hoping this helps others like myself who are reading the reviews.Ok, so the most important context is what phone I'm coming from over to the A17 5g. My old phone was Samsung A13 5g. My opinions of the new phone will be largely based on how they compare to the previous phone I used. So it's budget phone to budget phone, with the A17 having approximately 3-4ish years newer tech (or same tech but cheaper.) Both phones are being used on metro PCS (T mobile) network.So I've now had the A17 for exactly one week. I primarily use my phone for android auto, text, checking email, web browser, occasional YouTube and maybe once per week on some games. I don't use it for heavy loads like massive file transfers or rendering video. It's fairly light use overall.So far, the things I've been most pleased with are the screen and software/system layout. The screen has decent color and brightness and is MUCH better than the A13. Both screens claim to run at 90hz but the change from the old 270 PPI (I believe stands for pixel per inch or some equivalent) to 385 PPI feels massive. Much cleaner image from text to images. The change from LCD to AMOLED gives much better contrast with deeper colors. The software and system layout are a bit harder to describe in detail. It's more of a personal/ascetic preference. Things look and feel a lot cleaner. There are added optional features like side slide tabs to house shortcuts for certain apps. Another feature is top down swipe from the right for system shortcuts and from the left for notification, so they are smashed together.Another improvement, though less so than the screen and software changes, is in the speed and responsiveness of the phone. This one also needs to be put in context a bit. I'm sure some would complain about it while coming from a more expensive and technologically superior phone. I have my own bias, as I'm coming from an inferior phone which had over 3 years of use (slowing it down over time.) I also use it for mostly light tasks. That being said, I am pleased that the phone is noticeably more responsive than my old one. Most of the lagging happens on start up (goes away after a few mins while the phone is connecting a bunch of apps and putting out/requesting info like date/time/location.) When I booted it for the first time, that was the worst lag I had. It will also slow down if you have several apps running at the same time.  I feel like that's obvious, but some people genuinely don't know that if you hit the home button to leave an app, you need to bring up multi view and actually swipe the box away to close it fully. If you never close apps and never restart your phone on occasion it WILL slow way down. While using the phone for max 1 or 2 things at time it runs perfectly fine, and is better than the A13.Battery life is good. I went from appx. 5000mAh to 5000mAh phones, so besides the slight degradation in the old phones battery life it should be the same. 5000mAh for my uses feels excellent overall. It can go for a full 2 days without charging. Charging speed itself seems improved, but that's never mattered too much for me so I can't comment much. Seems fine though, roughly 1.5h charge from mostly dead to full. That's using a 25w fast charger block and appropriate USB c cable. I didn't use the cable that came with the phone so I can't comment. It didn't come with a charger block, by design. Your mileage on charge speed will vary based on what you're using to charge the phone with. The phone can't charge at full speed if you're using a 5w charger from 15 years ago.I don't have much to say about the camera. I rarely take photos and when I do it's usually quick snap shots of paper instructions or to share location. I believe (though I'm not sure) the A13 was also 50mp front camera but either the the other 2 lenses have been upgraded or they improved the camera software, because pictures do look a bit cleaner. It's not night and day or anything, but it looks better to my eye. Camera is also faster to adjust light and contrast when first focusing on a object, as compared to the old A13.Build quality seems a little improved. They are both budget phones and how build quality "feels" is inherently subjective but to me it does seem a little better.A quick note on activating this new phone...this may only be an issue I personally had, but in case this helps someone else I'd like to include it. I had a bit of trouble switching my physical SIM card out of my old phone and into the new. The metro app was telling me the phone wouldn't be compatible unless I changed phone plans (which is BS.) I had to call customer service and they opted to use the eSiM feature, rather than swapping the physical Sim. I noticed they also used the new phones 2nd SIM number to activate it, while i had tried using first. If you're having trouble perhaps check the phones info from the settings menu, and then try eSIM activation using the 2nd address. It worked fine for me after this.Samsung has a quick transfer feature if your previous phone was a Samsung. It basically copies over everything from your old phone, including apps, pictures, contacts and even text message history ect. It took 3 or 4 attempts (it didn't want to connect and dropped the connection once at 30% complete.) Luckily if it disconnects part way through, it will pick up where it left off, without needing to restart. Once it finally had a stable connection it took me about 6 minutes, it will vary based on how much stuff you have to move over. You need to download an app to do the transfer, but it will prompt you and take you to it's link.Summery: I find it pretty impressive how nice this phone feels both compared to its older model and for its price point in general. I found it frustrating that people would say this part or that was crap or great, but without giving any context to what they based that opinion off of. In my opinion, based on how cheap this phone is and compared to its older model (A13) this is an awesome phone so far, being one week in. Screen is a big improvement, system software and layout is better (IMO) and they seem to be making incremental improvements to things like the camera and overall build. For this price point I find it really impressive what you actually get. If you're coming from an older mid range phone I expect it will either be inferior or about the same. If you're coming from another phone in the 200 range it should be decent to good. For less than 200 and for what I use it for though, I'm very happy I bought this phone.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great Features and Value, But Smart Switch Had Issues
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: While the phone setup had a major hiccup, the overall experience has been excellent.The Setup Headache (Data Transfer)Setting up the phone and transferring data from the old device was a bit confusing and frustrating. The transfer app kept insisting on an update, but the download would just sit on "pending" forever and never actually progress. After wasting some time waiting, we finally aborted the automated transfer and did everything manually. If you run into the same issue, saving yourself the headache and going the manual route from the start might be faster.The Good Stuff: Features & PerformanceOnce the manual setup was done, the actual user experience has been fantastic. For the price, this phone is packed with incredible value and high-end features:Built-in AI Assistants: Having both the Gemini app and Microsoft Copilot ready to go right out of the box is incredibly convenient for quick searches, drafting, and productivity.Smart Camera Features: The hand recognition for selfies is a game-changer. You just show your palm to the camera, and it triggers the timer—no more awkward stretching to hit the shutter button.Excellent Value: Despite the initial software download glitch during setup, the phone itself offers a ton of modern functionality that makes it very worth the money.The VerdictThe phone itself is a 5-star device for features and value, but I'm knocking off one star due to the frustrating data transfer glitch. If you don't mind a little manual setup, it is a fantastic, feature-rich phone that won't break the bank!

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I got this to replace a Samsung A50 that was purchased in October 2019. Yes, 2019! That's before the world changed forever due to a pandemic. And that alone should tell you how infrequently I change phones and what my priorities in life are. I'm a simple woman with simple needs.There wasn't anything really wrong with my old phone but t unfortunately I cracked the screen and it was almost as much to fix it as it was to get a new one. So since it was practically a dinosaur I chose to "upgrade" and decided to take the chance on getting this model after doing a lot of research. I didn't want to spend a lot of money because I mainly use my phone for basic tasks, talking, texting, etc. I don't do any gaming, heavy streaming or lots of downloading. At most I'll watch a YT video or scroll sparingly on SM if time permits.It arrived quickly and came unlocked as described. That's about it for positive feedback. It was really surprising to me that this phone didn't perform nearly as well as it's almost 7 year old predecessor. Let's start with the fact that it took over 4 hours to do a transfer at the mobile store. Then I learned I really didn't have enough storage so a lot of my texts didn't transfer over. The next thing is I keep running out of space and have to keep deleting photos & videos. Now keep in mind these are the same photos from my old A50. I also have almost the same specs on this phone as there is on the A50 so I don't understand why this is happening.Yes, I know things change but I'm not a fan of the new texting features. They're so annoying, especially auto-correct and the "typing" bubble like the iPhone. And I don't find this to be very intuitive so I have trouble changing certain features easily. I have to dig and dig to find what I need.The UI (?) updates are constant and very annoying. Internet pages or tabs will close or switch for no reason and the phone is also laggy as heck. For example, sometimes it takes at least 4-7 seconds to capture a screenshot. Or at times there's a long delay to move from one part of an Internet page to another. What's crazy is I'm not the type of user who requires everything on my phone to move at the speed of light. I can accept a delay here or there but it's a constant waiting game with this phone. And don't get me started on how terrible the camera is. I absolutely despise every picture this camera takes and selfie are the worst! They have everyone looking haggard as heck, no matter what the setting. My A50 camera was 1000x better than this and I could always find a way to take a flattering photo.When I initially read all the negative reviews (and I mean ALL) I incorrectly assumed some of complaints were from folks who were used to swapping out their $2K phones every year. They had high standards and this is a low budget phone so they were disappointed. I get it. It's hard to enjoy beer when you have champagne tastes. But I was quite mistaken. A lot of the complaints are very valid and quite accurate.If you're looking for quality on a budget this ain't it. Trust me. This phone is probably best for a 10-year old child. Take it from someone with super low standards and who kept their own phone for an actual child's formative years. I'll keep it because I don't want to spend more money right now but do yourself a favor and keep your expectations low. If you need a high performance phone look elsewhere. I wish I did.

features: VERSATILE & EASY TO USE: With an upgraded height of 65 inches (165cm), our mobile stand adapts seamlessly to any crib, bassinet, or changing table. Its flexible design allows for easy adjustment and movement, making it perfect for creating a customized sleeping environment for your baby. You can also use this mobile hanger for crib to hang a mosquito net or other charming decorations!

SAFETY FIRST: We prioritize your baby's safety with a robust design featuring high-strength metal components and thickened 0.98 inch core wood poles. The square base ensures superior stability and grip, while the stand supports up to 3 lbs, making this baby crib mobile arm a reliable choice for your nursery.

The auto-off feature after 30 minutes helps save battery life. (Requires 2 AA batteries, not included.)

ALTERNATIVE USES: Get creative with our versatile baby mobile stand! Attach the baby music box to the crib or use it with brackets to hang your own toys. aPlusContent.title: Product description
aPlusContent.rawText:
Product description

We are a family-run business and are passionate about creating simple and adorable nursery decor. We aim to provide products that introduce your baby to soft, natural materials. We want to gently engage your little one with our products, and not overstimulate them! 
Exclusive artwork for Sorrel + Fern will add a dreamy look to your aviation themed nursery! 
FEATURES 
Made of premium quality felt and 100% natural unfinished wood. Wonderful, simple and unique room decor or gift for baby shower, birthday, or registry. 
Bring the skies inside with this serene airplane themed baby mobile! The gray, blue, and wooden planes with the cloud come together to make this aviation dream complete! 
This mobile is perfect for parents who are looking for a timeless design that will complement any nursery decor. 
EACH MOBILE INCLUDES 
1x White cloud 
1x Ceiling hook 
3x Navy blue airplanes 
3x Gray airplanes 
3x Tan airplanes 
Colors: Gray, White, Navy Blue, Tan 
MORE FEATURES 
SIMPLE AND MODERN 
This felt and wood mobile is made with a unique 3-D design that not only makes it adorable from an adults perspective, but, also interesting from the babies view. 
BEST PAIRED WITH SORREL + FERN'S CRIB ARM 
Complete the perfect nursery setup with our matching baby mobile and crib arm. Together they create a dynamic display above the crib, providing a safe and soothing visual for your little one. 
DESIGNED TO SOOTHE 
All Sorrel + Fern mobiles gently allow your little one to focus on natural materials while falling asleep. The mobile’s gentle movement and soft, soothing colors are carefully crafted to promote relaxation and aid in sleep. 
Fill your world with beauty by mix and matching with Sorrel + Fern’s crib arm. 
You can pair this Airplanes and Cloud baby mobile with our sturdy, natural, and lovely crib arm. 
Sorrel + Fern Crib Arm 
Made of beautiful, lightweight beechwood. Our crib arm will add natural beauty to any nursery. Its minimalist and classic wooden design make it perfect for any crib mobile theme. 
Easy to assemble and disassemble allowing you to easily pack away to save for future babies. 
OUR OTHER PRODUCTS THAT YOU MIGHT LIKE 
Thank you so much for stopping by! Below you will find some of our other products that we think you'll love!

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: For starters; the price on these phones is great. Between having the reassurance of Amazon buyer protection, and the benefit of knowing the device has been tested for performance, it’s well worth it.I needed a new phone fast after my cat knocked mine  into the sink ☹️ Rice fixed it for a while, but it was only temporary before it died altogether.I hate buying phones and avoid it whenever possible. 99% of mine belonged to someone in my family first. And i was good with that. Needless to say, my cat didn’t wait for someone in my family to upgrade. I was on my own this time.Okay.... that’s not entirely true. My grandma had an iPhone 7 sitting around so that held me over in the meantime. Going from an iPhone 11 Pro Max to an iPhone 7 was….bad. It was too dam small, in every possible way.  32 gigs of memory!! I needed an upgrade. Fast. My 11 year old was bullying me relentlessly. And that’s on me. They had my old XR (formerly my dad’s)I scoured FB marketplace. I’d decided upgrade a little, so I could feel better about the switch.  I didn’t want to feel backed me into a corner by my cat’s recklessness. I would get a slightly newer model in a fun colour.Marketplace had plenty.  Sending message after message from my iPhone 7, I worried. “This person seems too eager”, “this one has been posted so long”, “I want a purple, but the only purple one listed has less storage space” and “the pretty green one has a small crack”, “this guy lives 2 hours from me” and “Battery life? Errr last time I checked it was like 74%?….no, I can’t take a screenshot of it, it’s turned off”…. “cash only please” Etc.So much pressure. What happens if the thing doesn’t work? That’s $300+ down the drain. I knew I couldn’t afford new. But I hated the idea of buying something used from a stranger on Facebook. I didn’t want to get scammed, and I also didn’t want to settle.That’s when I remembered good ol’ Amazon. Maybe I’d check there. Just for funsies. Probably out of my budget, but it couldn’t hurt.Sure enough, refurbished devices selling “like new!” Mostly same cost or less than what I’d found so far. Surely there was a catch? I read through everything, tested by Amazon, includes all the specs, unlocked, I can pick the colour, the storage size, the condition, etc. AND I could have it delivered to me tomorrow??! With a warranty?!!I recovered from my brief stint of disappointment after learning the 12’s don’t come in yellow. Then fought hard to decide between mint and lavender. The lavender would take an extra day to arrive. Mint it was!!As promised, it arrived the next day. It was in beautiful shape. 128g’s, mint green, not a single scratch, 86% battery life. All for less than I would have paid to some stranger for a 64g with some “small scratches”Once my case and screen protector arrived I excitedly set it up and synced my data.Oh no.The FACE ID DIDNT WORK 😭After becoming used to facial recognition, having that yanked away, and dealing with a 7 for over 2 weeks—  I was desperate for the convenience of Face ID. I had been using my fingerprint. Like a *caveman*.Not to mention I have Blink 182 tickets, and it specifically states facial recognition is required to access the mobile tickets. Idk if that’s true, but I needed Face ID!!I googled, I contacted apple support. Fixing it could be upwards of $300. That’s almost what I paid for the whole phone!!I realllllly didn’t want to be stuck without a phone again. But I also wanted one fully functioning.So I reached out to Amazon support and explained. The rep was incredibly helpful (as most Amazon reps are) and after bts failed, she advised the ship was a 3rd party seller, and she  send a message to them. “If they don’t fix it by (insert date) contact us back and we’ll make this right” she encouraged.I’m ngl. I was nervous. I didn’t have high hopes, having dealt with 3p sellers on Amazon in the past. At least Amazon had my back, ig. The concert wasn’t till July. Even without facial recognition, it was loads better than the  7. I could make do in the meantime.The seller came in clutch though, and my worry was unwarranted. They responded within minutes. They were receptive, apologetic, and more than willing to help.As I’d anticipated, they offered a refund or exchange, as soon as they received the return. I explained my concern with not having a phone for several days or more; and the merchant offered to overnight a replacement as soon as the return was dropped off.I could deal with one day without a phone! I gratefully accepted. That was Saturday night, we made plans to catch up Monday for the return instructions and for them to overnight it.Monday I reached back out; and they were ready to ship, BUT they *had no more green….* 🫢 SHOCK“…do you have purple”No. :( just blue, white, and black.THIS WAS A HUGE BUMMER.It’s silly I know, and the definition of *first world problems “.. but I mean…. My change of heart about this whole phone thing HINGED ON THE FUN COLOUR. Without it, I was just a person…out $350… because my cat was thirsty while I was watching YouTube while washing dishes. I needed a cool colour. Plus,  I’d already gotten the matching case! Clear with mint green borders.It wasn’t even a fun blue… it was a dark, serious, navy blue. It was pretty and classy, but I wanted something fun. I even asked if he had any older models in yellow 😭😭 no luck,They told me they’d be restocking in a day or so. Still, no greens or purples came in.Ugh. Reality was setting in. I was going to have to settle. It was fine, I thought. At least it would be a fully functioning phone.No. I wasn’t ready to let go. They assured me I could take my time to decide, and I asked if we could wait another week in case one came in. If it didn’t, *then* I would choose from the options available.I messaged them Wednesday afternoon, bracing myself for the answer…. THEY GOT IN PURPLE! YAY.They sent a label, I dropped it off, sent a photo, and had my new phone the next morning.they’d said overnight shipping… but wow! I’d dropped off the return around 3pm, and had the replacement by noon the next day. I didn’t even have my new case yet 😅Despite the Barney-Esque colour scheme my mint green case created, the lavender is GORGEOUS and I’m actually sort of glad the green didn’t work out.Don’t get me wrong, the green is also  gorgeous.. but in the end I’m glad I ended up with the lavender. I was overjoyed when I was prompted to set Face ID during setup. Worked brilliantly, as did everything else.Great packaging, no cosmetic flaws, amazing battery life, customer service was great, and best of all… ITS PURPLE!Can’t wait to pair it with the new case. I’m so glad I went this route where I have some peace of mind as a buyer.I’m grateful to the seller for being so helpful and patient with me as insufferable as I must have seemed making such a fuss over colour preferenceIf you’re nervous buying a phone used or refurbished too, hopefully you can take comfort in knowing- this seller is legit. You receive a good quality product, and, speaking from experience, they’ll gladly help resolve any issues you may run into.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewTitle: Ottimo equilibrio tra prezzo e prestazioni
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: Ho acquistato questo Samsung Galaxy A16 4G LTE con un obiettivo molto semplice: trovare uno smartphone che fosse concreto, affidabile nell’uso quotidiano e, soprattutto, con un rapporto qualità prezzo convincente. Dopo averlo provato per un po’, posso dire che la sensazione generale è stata proprio quella di aver fatto una scelta sensata. Non cercavo un telefono da far “notare”, ma un dispositivo che mi accompagnasse nelle attività di tutti i giorni senza darmi la percezione di aver speso più del necessario rispetto a quello che offre.La prima impressione è stata positiva già dal momento in cui ho iniziato a usarlo. Si capisce subito che si tratta di un prodotto pensato per chi vuole qualcosa di pratico, senza complicazioni inutili. Il fatto che sia un dual SIM, per me, è stato un elemento utile perché aggiunge flessibilità nella gestione delle due linee. Anche la presenza di 4GB di RAM e 128GB di memoria mi è sembrata una combinazione equilibrata per questa fascia, soprattutto se si cerca un telefono essenziale ma con un margine di utilizzo abbastanza tranquillo nella vita di tutti i giorni.Quello che mi ha convinto di più, però, è l’insieme. Non ho avuto la sensazione di trovarmi davanti a un prodotto costruito al risparmio in modo evidente, ma a un modello che cerca un buon compromesso tra dotazione e spesa. In questa fascia, per me, conta molto che il telefono risulti coerente con quello che promette, e in questo caso la sensazione è stata quella giusta. Non ho avuto aspettative irrealistiche, e proprio per questo sono riuscito ad apprezzarlo di più: fa quello che deve fare, in modo semplice e diretto, senza far rimpiangere scelte più costose se l’uso richiesto è quello normale di un utente non troppo esigente.Anche esteticamente, nella versione nera, mi è sembrato sobrio e adatto a chi preferisce un dispositivo discreto. Non è un telefono che punta a stupire, ma a essere utilizzato con naturalezza. Questo per me è un punto a favore, perché spesso si tende a cercare caratteristiche spettacolari che poi, nell’uso reale, non incidono davvero quanto un equilibrio generale ben riuscito. Invece qui ho avuto l’impressione di un modello pensato con un criterio pratico, e questo lo rende facile da consigliare a chi vuole un acquisto ragionato.Naturalmente, quando si sceglie un prodotto di questo tipo, bisogna anche essere onesti su ciò che ci si aspetta. Io non lo vedo come la scelta per chi cerca il massimo in assoluto sotto ogni aspetto, ma come una soluzione molto valida per chi dà priorità alla convenienza concreta. È proprio in questo senso che mi ha soddisfatto: non promette più di quello che può offrire, e anzi riesce a trasmettere una sensazione di ordine e coerenza che, per me, vale molto più di tante promesse generiche.Un altro elemento che ho apprezzato è la semplicità con cui entra nella routine quotidiana. Quando un telefono non complica le cose, il suo valore cresce, soprattutto per chi desidera usarlo senza doverci pensare troppo. In questo caso, la dotazione generale mi è sembrata ben calibrata per un utilizzo normale, e la memoria interna da 128GB dà una base interessante per chi ha bisogno di spazio senza voler salire su modelli più impegnativi. Anche qui, il punto non è stupire, ma risultare utile in modo concreto.In definitiva, per me questo Samsung Galaxy A16 4G LTE merita pienamente il voto massimo perché rappresenta bene l’idea di miglior rapporto qualità prezzo. Non lo dico in modo superficiale: lo dico perché, per quello che offre e per come si presenta nell’uso quotidiano, mi ha dato esattamente la sensazione che cercavo. È uno smartphone che consiglierei a chi vuole un cellulare affidabile, essenziale e ben bilanciato, senza inseguire il superfluo. Se l’obiettivo è fare una scelta intelligente, mi sembra davvero centrato.
Ich habe 89€ bezahlt und das Handy ist echt Klasse!Hat alles was man braucht und ein echtes Schnäppchen!

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Some Cute Features, but Weak Build and Compatibility Issues
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This mobile has some nice visual and musical features, but the overall build quality left a lot to be desired. The plastic feels weak, and the weight of the mobile causes the arm to droop—enough that we were worried it could fall on our baby. The clamp base isn’t strong either and slips off most surfaces, so we ended up removing it altogether.We salvaged the mobile portion by attaching it elsewhere with zip ties, which worked better for us. The remote control operates on a generic frequency and ended up triggering other baby gear in our home, like our bassinet, which was frustrating.The LED projection is very faint—barely visible on the ceiling unless the room is completely dark, so don’t expect much from it in low-light conditions during the day. We even dropped the mobile once and it popped apart, though thankfully it snapped back together.It has some potential, but the weak materials and design flaws make it hard to recommend without modifications.

description: Product DescriptionIn Zeta Gundam, the sequel to the original Mobile Suit Gundam series, the Universal Century world is locked into an escalating conflict. While the AEUG resistance group strives to convince the world of the justice of its cause, the brutal Titans continue to suppress dissent through violence and fear. Now the struggle enters a new phase as a powerful third force enters the battlefield, and the AEUG and Titans race to enlist the support of the mysterious Axis renegades. Confronted with his past, Char Aznable at last decides to embrace his role as leader of the AEUG. But his choice may have come too late, for the Titans have completed their most terrible and devastating weapon.Amazon.comMobile Suit Zeta Gundam (1985) gets increasingly complicated, as Amuro Ray and Char Azanable from the first Gundam series appear. The confrontation between the rebel forces of the A.E.U.G. (Anti-Earth Union Group) and the power-hungry paramilitary Titans becomes a triangle of competing powers when a relict Zeon force arrives on the scene, led by Haman Karn, who is determined to restore the Zabi family to power. The storyline gets even more tangled as Kamille Bidan uses his Newtype powers to establish psychic bonds not only with his girlfriend Fa Yuiry, but with Sarah, Four, Reccoa, Emma, and Rosammy. These links feel repetitious, as do the metal-hand-to-metal-hand duels between Kamille's Zeta Gundam and the enemy Mobile Suits that occur in every episode. There's little sense of a broad story arc, and at this early phase of anime, the filmmakers were still learning how to write credible female characters. Fa comes across as a twit along the lines of Minmei in Robotech, and she's saddled with two thoroughly obnoxious orphans. Zeta Gundam lacks the depth of characterization that made 08 MS Team memorable and the CG-assisted space battles in Gundam Seed and other recent installments. But for viewers interested in following the development of the popular and long-running Gundam franchise, it's must viewing. (Rated 13 and older: violence, violence against women, nudity, alcohol use) --Charles Solomon

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Now, this here is the second half of Mobile Suit Zeta Gundam. As far as disk presentations go, it's solid. The case is large and boxy and contains five disks rounding out to 25 Episodes, along with Collection 1 this ends up at a 50 episode series, slightly longer than the original at 46.I prefer to relate this Anime to Angel, the spin-off of Buffy the Vampire Slayer. It's great, it's amazing, it contains more of your favorite characters, new interesting characters, it's a darker and more tragic story, and you really have to watch the original to get anything. Zeta Gundam has a high barrier of entry, and not everybody wants to spend 46 episodes of Original MSG to get into this.For those who do, you'll find an anime so great, to this day it spawns endless sequels, spin-off's, merchandise, and copycats.  This is an anime that spawned a Genre, and this is the grandest representation of that genre ever conceived.Animation wise, you'll have to realize this was done in the 80's. And that being said, it's fantastic. The best word to put to it is EFFORT...and buckets of cash. This series had a budget of Michel Bay levels, and it shows. The detail, the crisp and flowing animation. They don't take too many short cuts and the designs arn't too outlandish. Everything feels like and acts like it works. No skimping, when that robot loses an arm he loses and arm, it's not just some electricy-thing...no, they put WORK into this show, you can tell. Dis ain't no 12 episode wanta-be mecha with stock footage, it's serious business.The overarching plot of Zeta Gundam revolves around it's characters. As a War drama, our giant robot's here arn't robotic partners helping our heroes defeat the bad guys, they're vehicles, or more simply, weapons.  Robots kill, they break, they need to be repaired. This show has robots in it, but you're not here simply for the robots. It's these characters, and I'm going to outline the two stand out villains. Paptimus Scirocco and Lady Haman. They're practically opposites. A man who believe himself a genius, and thinks everyone else are simply tools for his use. Now, he intends to use these people(tools) to change the world for perhaps the better, but the way he goes about things is a bit...misogynistic. He's pretty fond of wooing women and well, using them.  Then you got Lady Haman, who's like a sexy charismatic female version of Hitler...or perhaps Stalin...I'm not sure.  She's powerful, respected, intelligent, and has a clear goal in which she's driven for. She's a villain you don't get often. How often are women such strong characters such as this?  She's not crazy, or love struck or MWUAHAHA evil, she's focused on rebuilding the family Empire, what's wrong with that...other than that empire being a bunch of racist sociopaths with extremist ideals.Now, put these two villains against each other, add in a corrupt Government opposed to both, and a Rebel faction EXTREMELY opposed to the corrupt Government, and you have yourself an interesting and extremely difficult to understand from the outside viewer Plot!This show has far better reviews from far better writers than me, but if you're reading this, I say check it out, you won't regret it.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Tons of positives, a few negatives, but when it all boils down...
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: ...this is without a doubt the best Gundam series I've ever seen. So far it's the only one I've actually liked enough to BUY the whole thing. Some problems do weigh this show down a little bit, but with the legion of positives, it almost doesn't matter.POSITIVES:+ Characters are full of personality; good characters aren't all justice, all the time; evil characters are not MWAHAHAHAHA TAKE OVER TEH WORLD evil and each has their own unique characteristics.+ Rather than have a share of iffy episodes thrown in with some magnificent ones, the show never strays from telling a full-on story.+ Tons of plot-twists; not a boring and predictable storyline.+ Music is relatively simple in composition, but adds depth and gives a retro feel.+ Characters from the original Gundam make more than just cameo appearances; several such as Amuro, Hayato, Katz, Char, and Bright play significant roles in the story, while Kai, Mirai, and Fraw play good brief supporting roles. The only one to make merely a cameo appearance and not even say anything is Sayla.+ While not continuing right where the first Gundam series left off, the connections to the original are very well planned.NEGATIVES (Because nothing's really perfect)- Sometimes when a character doesn't show up for a while, you think "Where did he/she go?" and when they return again you think "How did he/she get here of all places?"- This is 1985, so the art and animation are a little dated.- The dub is pretty bad.- Kamille, while not boring, is sometimes a very annoying, Luke Skywalker-level whiny lead character.The thing is, not only are there more good things than bad, the good things would outweigh the bad if there were the same number of each. This show simply cannot be missed. BUT! At the same time, it is better you see some fair portion of the first Gundam series, either in the 43 television episodes or the three compilation movies. That way, you will have a significantly better understanding of some of the names and terminology used in this show. 5 stars all the way!

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: A great phone...but compared to what?
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Tldr: Good phone for this price, noticeably better than older A13 and I wish more people would include context to their reviews. Glad I bought mine.I'm leaving a long and detailed review because I got tired of reading through reviews that seemed contradictory, or said something was "bad" but without any context. If I made a poor choice buying a phone I'd likely be stuck with it for some years. I'm hoping this helps others like myself who are reading the reviews.Ok, so the most important context is what phone I'm coming from over to the A17 5g. My old phone was Samsung A13 5g. My opinions of the new phone will be largely based on how they compare to the previous phone I used. So it's budget phone to budget phone, with the A17 having approximately 3-4ish years newer tech (or same tech but cheaper.) Both phones are being used on metro PCS (T mobile) network.So I've now had the A17 for exactly one week. I primarily use my phone for android auto, text, checking email, web browser, occasional YouTube and maybe once per week on some games. I don't use it for heavy loads like massive file transfers or rendering video. It's fairly light use overall.So far, the things I've been most pleased with are the screen and software/system layout. The screen has decent color and brightness and is MUCH better than the A13. Both screens claim to run at 90hz but the change from the old 270 PPI (I believe stands for pixel per inch or some equivalent) to 385 PPI feels massive. Much cleaner image from text to images. The change from LCD to AMOLED gives much better contrast with deeper colors. The software and system layout are a bit harder to describe in detail. It's more of a personal/ascetic preference. Things look and feel a lot cleaner. There are added optional features like side slide tabs to house shortcuts for certain apps. Another feature is top down swipe from the right for system shortcuts and from the left for notification, so they are smashed together.Another improvement, though less so than the screen and software changes, is in the speed and responsiveness of the phone. This one also needs to be put in context a bit. I'm sure some would complain about it while coming from a more expensive and technologically superior phone. I have my own bias, as I'm coming from an inferior phone which had over 3 years of use (slowing it down over time.) I also use it for mostly light tasks. That being said, I am pleased that the phone is noticeably more responsive than my old one. Most of the lagging happens on start up (goes away after a few mins while the phone is connecting a bunch of apps and putting out/requesting info like date/time/location.) When I booted it for the first time, that was the worst lag I had. It will also slow down if you have several apps running at the same time.  I feel like that's obvious, but some people genuinely don't know that if you hit the home button to leave an app, you need to bring up multi view and actually swipe the box away to close it fully. If you never close apps and never restart your phone on occasion it WILL slow way down. While using the phone for max 1 or 2 things at time it runs perfectly fine, and is better than the A13.Battery life is good. I went from appx. 5000mAh to 5000mAh phones, so besides the slight degradation in the old phones battery life it should be the same. 5000mAh for my uses feels excellent overall. It can go for a full 2 days without charging. Charging speed itself seems improved, but that's never mattered too much for me so I can't comment much. Seems fine though, roughly 1.5h charge from mostly dead to full. That's using a 25w fast charger block and appropriate USB c cable. I didn't use the cable that came with the phone so I can't comment. It didn't come with a charger block, by design. Your mileage on charge speed will vary based on what you're using to charge the phone with. The phone can't charge at full speed if you're using a 5w charger from 15 years ago.I don't have much to say about the camera. I rarely take photos and when I do it's usually quick snap shots of paper instructions or to share location. I believe (though I'm not sure) the A13 was also 50mp front camera but either the the other 2 lenses have been upgraded or they improved the camera software, because pictures do look a bit cleaner. It's not night and day or anything, but it looks better to my eye. Camera is also faster to adjust light and contrast when first focusing on a object, as compared to the old A13.Build quality seems a little improved. They are both budget phones and how build quality "feels" is inherently subjective but to me it does seem a little better.A quick note on activating this new phone...this may only be an issue I personally had, but in case this helps someone else I'd like to include it. I had a bit of trouble switching my physical SIM card out of my old phone and into the new. The metro app was telling me the phone wouldn't be compatible unless I changed phone plans (which is BS.) I had to call customer service and they opted to use the eSiM feature, rather than swapping the physical Sim. I noticed they also used the new phones 2nd SIM number to activate it, while i had tried using first. If you're having trouble perhaps check the phones info from the settings menu, and then try eSIM activation using the 2nd address. It worked fine for me after this.Samsung has a quick transfer feature if your previous phone was a Samsung. It basically copies over everything from your old phone, including apps, pictures, contacts and even text message history ect. It took 3 or 4 attempts (it didn't want to connect and dropped the connection once at 30% complete.) Luckily if it disconnects part way through, it will pick up where it left off, without needing to restart. Once it finally had a stable connection it took me about 6 minutes, it will vary based on how much stuff you have to move over. You need to download an app to do the transfer, but it will prompt you and take you to it's link.Summery: I find it pretty impressive how nice this phone feels both compared to its older model and for its price point in general. I found it frustrating that people would say this part or that was crap or great, but without giving any context to what they based that opinion off of. In my opinion, based on how cheap this phone is and compared to its older model (A13) this is an awesome phone so far, being one week in. Screen is a big improvement, system software and layout is better (IMO) and they seem to be making incremental improvements to things like the camera and overall build. For this price point I find it really impressive what you actually get. If you're coming from an older mid range phone I expect it will either be inferior or about the same. If you're coming from another phone in the 200 range it should be decent to good. For less than 200 and for what I use it for though, I'm very happy I bought this phone.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great Features and Value, But Smart Switch Had Issues
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: While the phone setup had a major hiccup, the overall experience has been excellent.The Setup Headache (Data Transfer)Setting up the phone and transferring data from the old device was a bit confusing and frustrating. The transfer app kept insisting on an update, but the download would just sit on "pending" forever and never actually progress. After wasting some time waiting, we finally aborted the automated transfer and did everything manually. If you run into the same issue, saving yourself the headache and going the manual route from the start might be faster.The Good Stuff: Features & PerformanceOnce the manual setup was done, the actual user experience has been fantastic. For the price, this phone is packed with incredible value and high-end features:Built-in AI Assistants: Having both the Gemini app and Microsoft Copilot ready to go right out of the box is incredibly convenient for quick searches, drafting, and productivity.Smart Camera Features: The hand recognition for selfies is a game-changer. You just show your palm to the camera, and it triggers the timer—no more awkward stretching to hit the shutter button.Excellent Value: Despite the initial software download glitch during setup, the phone itself offers a ton of modern functionality that makes it very worth the money.The VerdictThe phone itself is a 5-star device for features and value, but I'm knocking off one star due to the frustrating data transfer glitch. If you don't mind a little manual setup, it is a fantastic, feature-rich phone that won't break the bank!

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I got this to replace a Samsung A50 that was purchased in October 2019. Yes, 2019! That's before the world changed forever due to a pandemic. And that alone should tell you how infrequently I change phones and what my priorities in life are. I'm a simple woman with simple needs.There wasn't anything really wrong with my old phone but t unfortunately I cracked the screen and it was almost as much to fix it as it was to get a new one. So since it was practically a dinosaur I chose to "upgrade" and decided to take the chance on getting this model after doing a lot of research. I didn't want to spend a lot of money because I mainly use my phone for basic tasks, talking, texting, etc. I don't do any gaming, heavy streaming or lots of downloading. At most I'll watch a YT video or scroll sparingly on SM if time permits.It arrived quickly and came unlocked as described. That's about it for positive feedback. It was really surprising to me that this phone didn't perform nearly as well as it's almost 7 year old predecessor. Let's start with the fact that it took over 4 hours to do a transfer at the mobile store. Then I learned I really didn't have enough storage so a lot of my texts didn't transfer over. The next thing is I keep running out of space and have to keep deleting photos & videos. Now keep in mind these are the same photos from my old A50. I also have almost the same specs on this phone as there is on the A50 so I don't understand why this is happening.Yes, I know things change but I'm not a fan of the new texting features. They're so annoying, especially auto-correct and the "typing" bubble like the iPhone. And I don't find this to be very intuitive so I have trouble changing certain features easily. I have to dig and dig to find what I need.The UI (?) updates are constant and very annoying. Internet pages or tabs will close or switch for no reason and the phone is also laggy as heck. For example, sometimes it takes at least 4-7 seconds to capture a screenshot. Or at times there's a long delay to move from one part of an Internet page to another. What's crazy is I'm not the type of user who requires everything on my phone to move at the speed of light. I can accept a delay here or there but it's a constant waiting game with this phone. And don't get me started on how terrible the camera is. I absolutely despise every picture this camera takes and selfie are the worst! They have everyone looking haggard as heck, no matter what the setting. My A50 camera was 1000x better than this and I could always find a way to take a flattering photo.When I initially read all the negative reviews (and I mean ALL) I incorrectly assumed some of complaints were from folks who were used to swapping out their $2K phones every year. They had high standards and this is a low budget phone so they were disappointed. I get it. It's hard to enjoy beer when you have champagne tastes. But I was quite mistaken. A lot of the complaints are very valid and quite accurate.If you're looking for quality on a budget this ain't it. Trust me. This phone is probably best for a 10-year old child. Take it from someone with super low standards and who kept their own phone for an actual child's formative years. I'll keep it because I don't want to spend more money right now but do yourself a favor and keep your expectations low. If you need a high performance phone look elsewhere. I wish I did.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: So I've always been skeptical of buying refurbished items but my sister did it so I kinda thought why not? I bought this from the seller Wireless Source back on the 17th and I and received it on the 20th. So it was delivered quickly. It came in a brown box with a printed stickt label detailing what's inside. Upon opening the box, the phone box was wrapped nicely in packaging. I was surprised the seller had placed the phone into another box but super glad they did because it was STROMING! After taking the phone out of the box, first impressions was DAMN! The color is gorgeous and slick, the seller already put on screen protector. It was pretty much brand new! It had no scratches, chips, missing piant, absolutely NOTHING. It came with a charger and the pin to open the sim card area. The phone did come in dead so I immediately placed it on the charger. After about an hour give or take (I went to Walmart so came back so now exactly sure when it was fully charged) it was charged, and I turned it on with no issues. I set up the photo manually which was super simple to do after I inserted my sim card. I didn't need a code or anything it just asked me if I wanted to use the Sims card or use a new one. Once I verified that I wanted to use the old Sims card, it immediately recognized it as AT&T and asked me to click okay to switch over. Done. All my apps are on and updated. Everything is set to my liking and I've had no issues at all. I've had the phone for 2 full days now and the phone actually automatically adjust the brighteness if you are outside or in a dim environment. Just be careful because you have to readjust the brightness whenever you like it after. The phone battery life is pretty darn good. I'm currently at 45% and it's 5:07pm where I'm located. The phone has been used actively since 8am off charger. The camera quality is fantastic. Volume and sound is phenomenal. There is lots of storage and I have plenty more of exploring to do on the phone. I have let the phone die and had no problems with charging and turning back on. It will let you add a fingerprint for protection later one which I thought was cool because I didn't have to set thay up right away. Samsung is just the best for that. I bought a case to match the phone as well. I absolutely love the phone so far.The only downside, in my opinion, is that I can not add an SD card. Other then that, it's an exceptional phone. I will definitely update later if anything starts happening or I find cool stuff regarding the phone but so far so good!

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: NOT FACTORY UNLOCKED! I didn't realize this immediately because it is not specifically sim-locked, and data and calling worked fine. Fast forward 6 months, I get an email from work telling me I'll be kicked off the MDM policy (work email on personal phone) unless I update my OS. Evidently it was a Verizon phone, which can only receive software updates if you have Verizon SIM card. I have spent days trying to get support from Samsung, Verizon, AT&T, Amazon, and the Amazon seller only to be told to pound sand >:[It would seem my only option now is to take a risk with leaked / pirated firmware flashing, which I'm worried will trip the Knox security (which is the only reason I bought the phone in the first place, as Knox security was required by my employer).The phone itself is also disappointing. I started with a OnePlus 5t, which I was very happy with. When I was required to get a Samsung, I went to an A52 5g. The fingerprint sensor and face recognition were both so bad that unlocking the phone was a massive chore (something I do dozens of times a day). I suffered through this for a little while before upgrading to the S22. I very much resent the trend of under-display sensors which do not perform as well as their more visible counterparts. The S22 ultrasonic fingerprint sensor is vastly better than the optical one on the A52, but it still is inferior compared to a sensor on the back of the phone like on my older OnePlus. Heck, even my old galaxy S5 had a better fingerprint sensor.The face detection is a little better than the A52, but not as good as the OnePlus 5t. It really struggles in low light, and must be directly in front of your face. Nobody does face detection as well as Apple, but that's probably due to patent limitations (and I refuse to go back to iphone until they allow sideloading).One notable issue both the A52 and S22 suffer is an inability to detect they are in my pocket. I must deliberately place the phone with the screen facing outwards or else the fingerprint reader will constantly register false attempts against my leg (which will lock you out of using biometrics)Battery life is not impressive. Once again the 5t was better. This may not be entirely fair b/c I do use the always-on display, but on the other hand the processor should be much more efficient for how much newer it is. I mostly believe this is similar to the issue of constantly waking up in my pocket. A proper proximity sensor could have solved this rather than just using the selfie camera, which is again another example of form over function (It also seems like samsung doesn't even attempt to detect being in you pocket in order to reduce battery / ignore touch screen).

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I waited for some time to leave this review as some customers stated that phones started working worse in a few months. While booting (which was done in the summer), the phone overheated, but it was a one-time thing that happened during the setup. The camera gets laggy and hot if in use for a long time(like a realllly long time). Overall, the CPU used with this model has the issue, so overheating is not a big deal or a surprise. During everyday life, it works great, takes good pictures, and sounds okay; the fingerprint sensor works fine, and so does the face recognition. The only thing I am not very sure of is if the phone is waterproof, but it's easy to check; I just need to meet a technician. Overall, it is a good product with enough value for the price. It came with a cable AND a charging block that gives super fast charging. I wasn't expecting it, but it was nice to get. Overall, battery life is okay; my previous phone worked almost the same, so nothing too bad for me. Also, I have turned on the battery limitation (it can only charge up to 85% now), and I still go through 2/3 of the day. I always have a charger by my side and never really drained the battery, but I guess it would go through the day with constant use.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Part of me feels guilty for assessing so critically. I have a hand-held computer in my pocket that functions far beyond what we could have hoped for a decade ago.Even so, this hasn't been an absolute win for me. This is my first Samsung phone in many years. I think the S4 or S5 may have been my last Galaxy. I've loved Moto phones for the last several years, and this definitely lacks some of the functionality that I've come to enjoy from Motorola: shaking for the flashlight, side button screenshots, hovering over for the time on lockscreen.The camera is an improvement over my Moto Z4. And the processor does seem to be quite effective. But the battery is far weaker than I was expecting, and I'm a little worried about how bad it may get after a year or two of use if it's this much of a challenge now (6 weeks of use). Additionally, the fingerprint sensor is very finicky. I'm guessing I have about a 30% success rate with it. I have a screen protector on, which may be a factor, but it's the same brand of protector that I have used for years without issue on my Motos. (And I did try another brand of protector, but it brought the success rate down to about 5%.)Set-up was more challenging than Moto set ups are. The Samsung app promised to reset my screen and everything, but I had to manually set it up after running the Samsung setup process. Perhaps it was challenged by having to move from a different brand, but I wasn't impressed. Samsung is supposed to be top of the line for Android, but I'll be seriously considering other options when this wears out. My hope is that Moto will catch up to industry standards, but if not, I may be willing to accept a slower processor in exchange for a better overall user experience. If I change my mind, I'll come back and update this review.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewTitle: Excellent refurbished phone; great phone for the price
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: Refurbished phone is in excellent condition. Everything works as it should; phone was unlocked; phone readily worked with my Koodo SIM card. Some minor blemishes at the top right corner of the side of the phone are the only hint that this is a refurbished phone; I'm not at all concerned about these marks as the phone is going into a case. Screen and audio are perfect; wireless charging works; USB charging works. The S22 gets a bad rap for battery life but my battery has been just fine. Now, I don't take selfies every few minutes; I don't photograph every meal; I don't tweet or post or stream while walking or driving -- so maybe my use is a little lightweight compared to what the skibidi rizzler kids are doing these days (yo). Battery typically handles two days of of normal use. When I transferred data from my old phone, the S22 did get warm and you could actually watch the battery percentage tick down as the phones ultrasonically spoke with one another. Several Android updates installed themselves during initial setup, and again the phone got warm and used a lot of battery. I am guessing that was some pretty intense activity, as after that the phone has not gotten warm during anything I've been doing and battery life has been excellent. Am only disappointed with one thing: Samsung fakes moon photos. I tried taking photos of a recent full moon without a tripod. Holding the phone by hand, I zoomed in on the moon. The moon was an unfocused blur for most of the photos. But then, once after zooming, the moon suddenly snapped from an unfocused blob into a sharp image. The change on the screen was surprising -- it was very sudden, very unlike the slow sharpening of an image coming into focus: one moment the moon was a blob, then *SNAP!* it was a clear image. Totes fake and Samsung should be ashamed of themselves for pulling this sort of nonsense. If I find out that my photos of the northern lights are fake, I'm going to be really cheesed off. That's my only disappointment with the phone -- lunar photo fakery. Shame, Samsung, shame.  Other than that, am very pleased with the phone and the seller -- highly recommended.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Good inexpensive alternative to mainstream cellular providers.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This is a no brainier for unlimited voice/text/internet over 3 months. Then you have to re-up for 6 months or a year to get this price. Notice I said internet and not data. While internet is data you won't be able to use your phone as a hotspot. While they advertise that as being included. I have yet to get it to work on a Galaxy S-21 Ultra 5G, or a TCL-40 XL 5G. In spite of the recommendations from Mint Mobile Text Support Reps. I'm sure this could be fixed by a technician at a physical store location, but where are they and who has time for that. Finally it's not like there aren't other options. Excluding that minor irritation the service has been awesome! No dropped calls, telemarketers, or excess throttling, mater of fact I haven't noticed any throttling the 3 months I have had Mint Mobile. Their application is more of an upsell platform than anything else. But there text tech support is responsive and tries their best to be helpful. So if you don't care about having a hot spot. Are willing to pay as you go quarterly at best, not monthly, Mint Mobile may be for you. Especially if you can pay by the year!

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I was able to change my provider to Mint, keep my phone number and have it ported, and make a phone call in less than an hour with this package. I was paying four times that with Verizon for 3 years plus more for my tablet. I will never do that again! I always wanted the option to get a discount for paying multiple months which no other company currently offers.The only downside is the data caps, but even they aren't significant. The data speeds are about the same as Verizon at a quarter of the cost. I haven't had issues with dropped calls caused by this provider. The connection issues are local and specific to my local home area and have happened with every major provider.I am happy with my service and look forward to snagging another deal to continue service when my 3 months are over.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I honestly cannot recommend this phone at ALL!!!! I have broken down into numerous issues below:First for the positives: There are so few and far between... The included phone case is actually nice and works well, although is a fingerprint magnet. The screen can get nice and bright, and does have some decent clarity to it. The speakers are pretty good for as cheap as the device is. Honestly thats about it, now for the negatives...Performance: To say this thing is a potato would be an understatement. The UI is laggy and slow at the very least, sometimes crashing multiple times performing simple tasks. Asking it to the change the background on the home screen would cause a crash, accessing settings would cause a crash, and simply restarting the phone would cause it to be so laggy for up to 5 minutes before it would respond properly. Signal is not the greatest, very spotty at times and would go from 5 bars to none for no reason randomly.UI (Operating System): Crashes all the time, laggy, and contains a ton (and I mean a ton) of bloatware. I finally had to disable Blu's "app store" completely, as everytime I would remove apps, more would suddenly and randomly get installed. I got to the point where almost everything except Spotify was either removed or disabled, and the UI still could not run properly.Battery: Battery while it seems large, actually does not perform as well as similar sized batteries. After a full charge, the battery was already down to 72% within 30 minutes just from using Spotify, even after removing all the bloatware. Charging is not great, even hooked up to a PD charger (capable of 120watts), would take over half an hour to even gain 5%.Memory: While internal memory did seem okay, I did decide to opt into an MicroSD card, so that I could download songs via Spotify, that was a HUGE mistake. It would work, but upon rebooting the phone, or heck even walking away for 10 minutes, the SD would dismount or something and completely wipe the card. It actually destroyed 2 MicroSD cards, due to being corrupted so bad that even a computer could not get them to reformat. Also, as a side note, for some reason everytime the screen would switch off due to inactivity, the downloads would stop, weird i know!Overall: Destroys SD Cards, slow and laggy performance, slow charging, weak battery, slow download, spotty network at best. Does have Okay speakers and screen, but performance can't correct for that.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: A good phone for the price but you must disable some apps
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: It's about as cheap a price as you can pay for an unlocked new smart phone, so you have to adjust your expectations for that. Given the price this phone performs excellently. Screen, battery life, camera,  and performance is all adequate. You probably won't be wanting to use the pictures the camera takes but it's perfectly acceptable for video calls. Yes there's frequent small lags on a phone this low end. I've used many low end androids over the years and they all have that issue. I don't expect to use this phone for more than a few months max, and it is a perfect fit for the short time I need it for. Again, don't expect to be wowd by anything for the price point, but it's all functionalFor the price I was almost willing to give it 5stars as the best unlocked, no carrier required phone for this price I've ever used. However it comes with some bloat ware apps that required downloading and system apps that I had to forcibly disable. That's why it's only getting 4 stars.A phone with such low powered performance and low storage shouldn't have to be pruned by the end user. Forced disabling of some apps will improve performance though so if you get this phone I suggest you disable these apps in your app settings immediately:AppServices, Google Partner Setup, Google Wi-fi Provisioner, Headlines, news., Private Compute Services.And uninstall any preloaded apps or apps that were forced to install before you were able to disable the above.Some above are disguised by name as necessary but they are just bloat ware.I'd suggest this phone for anyone wanting an android phone to hold them over until they get a proper phone. Or for any reason you'd want to quickly get a cheap burner phone for a few months. Well worth the 60USD price tag

bookDescription: Explore new movements and alleviate stiff joints with more than 100 exercises designed to keep you flexible, energized, and active for life. Pain and stiffness can create fear and uncertainty in our ability to move, affecting quality of life. Exercise has continuously proven to be beneficial against disease, yet people are becoming increasingly sedentary.More than a quarter of the world's population is insufficiently active and it's time we remove barriers to exercise and encourage movement exploration. The Science of Stretch is your guide to understanding the human body's resilient and adaptable nature and how stretching can play a role in achieving your highest well-being.Inside the pages of this book you'll learn about:-The latest research on stretching-Human anatomy and physiology-The nervous system and pain science-How to reduce injury risk with exercise-Managing a lifestyle catered towards healthy aging-What happens to the body when we stretch-Different types of stretching and how to implement them to best compliment your daily life or sporting activities-Finally, a series of suggested stretch routines are outlined, each with a progressive increase in challenge and tailored to different abilities and fitness objectives-alongside the tools to create your own bespoke workouts.Every exercise is anatomized in detail to make movement easily understood using CGI artworks to show how each muscle is correctly activated and each joint aligned. Whether you're taking a walk around the park or running a marathon, Science of Stretch will help you stay flexible, keep active, and remove the uncertainty from stretching.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I ordered an iPhone 14 Refurbished Excellent from Amazons Renewed store but the first one arrived marked (Refurbished Good) I could see some small scratches and the battery health was at the bare minimum of 80% when 99% of Refurbished sellers rate Renewed Excellent as cosmetically near perfect and minimum battery health 85%+ so after speaking with CS and supervisors over a 5 day period and being promised several different things like partial refund or replacement (None of which happened and I was starting to get upset as I have been a Prime member for over 20 years so I just returned it and ordered another one from the Amazon Renewed store but the next morning I recieved a message/email from Amazon saying that the replacement iPhone I just ordered was coming from a seller other then the one I ordered it from? productPageReviews.reviewTitle: 1st purchase was great! This one was not!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I have had this iPhone for 38 days.It has the worst battery life of any iPhone I've ever owned, and I have owned ONLY iPhones since the first version was released 17 years ago.This is the second iPhone 14 that I've bought from the renewed store .The first one I bought on December 4th, 2023, and I could not have been happier with the phone.It arrived in brand new condition, and performed flawlessly.On the recommendation of a friend, I checked the battery health and charging after having it for MONTHS and it was at 100%! I was thrilled!I absolutely loved the phone!I never had a single problem with it.Unfortunately, on July 30 of this year I dropped it, and it was beyond repair.I immediately went back to the Amazon renewed store and purchased another iPhone 14 because my experience with the first one was so fantastic.It arrived in new looking condition, exactly like the one I bought in December 2023.It was not scratched or anything really noticeable, it just seemed to be "worn" a little bit, but I fully understood that it was a renewed phone, and any cosmetic issues were not that important to me, including the color, which, when my iPhone is in its case, you cannot tell what color it is anyway.Unfortunately, I DID NOT look at the battery health and charging when I first got the phone 38 days ago, but I did look at it about two weeks ago, and it said 93%.I thought, ok, it's a renewed phone, it's not going to have 100% battery life.I can live with that.Well, I just looked at it today and it's now at 90% battery health and charging.So this phone is dying quickly.After being fully charged it dies within hours.I have it completely set up for optimized battery life.I have lost emails and messages that I was in the middle of composing, and the phone just dies.I've been in the middle of important phone calls when the phone dies, simply because I had just fully charged it a few hours before that, and thought I would be fine for hours to come.I just had a total shoulder replacement surgery a week ago, and I was on the phone with my doctors office yesterday about my first post-op appointment, and my phone died in the middle of it.I thought I had HOURS left before the phone would die.Then I had to plug it in, and wait for it to come back alive, so I could call my doctor back and hopefully not wait a half hour after losing my place in line.On top of that is also has issues with the touchscreen being glitchy, and sometimes I have to tap on things several times to get them to work.As I said, I have been an iPhone owner/user since the very first version came out 17 years ago.I've always loved all my iPhones, and I will continue to be an iPhone user for the rest of my life.This is in no way reflection on Apple iPhones whatsoever.They are an amazing and fantastic piece of technology.I think I just got a bad one for the first time in my life.Luckily, I have just checked and I have until November 6th to return this phone, and I WILL be returning it.The problem is, what do I do in the meantime?Am I expected to buy a new one and get that shipped to me, transfer all my information from this phone to the new one, and then return this one?That is extremely hard to do financially!I am actually still paying for this phone on my Amazon Prime American Express card!Or, do I return this phone and wait until the refund has been issued and then buy another phone? Then wait until that is sent to me.I would not have a phone for at least a week in the interim, and we all know these days that's a practical impossibility.I am also having several medical issues.Like I said, I just had a total shoulder replacement surgery last Monday, September 9th, and have several upcoming follow up appointments, and physical therapy appointments.I also have several other non-related medical issues that definitely require that I have a phone.I just don't know what to do.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: I took a chance and it worked out
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I have to say, I have charged this phone to 100% twice now (only have had the phone a few days). In standby for 24 hours, the phone only lost 16% charge. I was able to upgrade to iOS 26.I purchased this phone for traveling by plane. I don't want to bring my iPhone 15 so I needed at least an iPhone 14 for transferring the eSIM. This part I have not done yet because I'm not traveling for another month, but will update this review after my trip.Because it's a travel phone, I didn't want to sync anything, especially the passwords. I only wanted the phone for phone calls and messages. There wasn't an option when setting up the phone to skip syncing, only skipping back up. I had to stop the syncing in progress and delete what was synced. You must disable syncing before deleting else you may delete what's in the cloud.I was nervous about buying this based on the negative seller reviews. I typically don't purchase from third party sellers because returns can be difficult, as a lot of seller reviews noted. I saw one review that stated they were only able to get a full refund with photo proof and help from Amazon. So, I had the phone shipped to UPS and recorded the unboxing to alleviate any accusations that I, the customer, caused any damage. The phone looked fine. I purchased "excellent" condition, which speaks to the visible condition of the phone. I can see the scratch on the screen from more than a foot away, but my concern was more about the condition/performance of the phone.I wish Amazon would assist more with returns, as it seems many were left unsatisfied. I hope that my experience becomes more the norm. I had a lot of anxiety over this and I'm glad it worked out, but I feel it would be hit or miss in general if a return is needed.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This baby mobile is absolutely adorable and has a beautiful neutral color palette that fits perfectly with almost any nursery theme. The knitted animal designs are incredibly well made, with soft textures and charming details that make each piece stand out. I especially love the lion, panda, elephant, and bear, along with the fluffy cloud in the center. The natural wooden ring gives it a modern, high-quality look that feels both stylish and timeless.The mobile is lightweight, hangs evenly, and gently moves with air circulation, giving babies something calming to watch while lying in their crib. The craftsmanship is excellent, and everything feels securely attached and thoughtfully designed. It makes a wonderful nursery decoration while also providing gentle visual stimulation, and I’m very happy with the overall quality and appearance.The only downside is it doesn’t fit well on our bassinet so I had to retrofit to another piece of furniture next to it, a book shelf. It would fit more securely on a crib. Just want to warn others but it doesn’t really affect the use of it. Still love this thing.
