productPageReviews.reviewTitle: The Superior AR Dock VS the Competition
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Update 3/2/2026:I've most recently acquired the Xreal 1S and on that AR glasses it supports a feature to turn the screen into an ultrawide screen making the screen curve and extra wide. It seems however the Pro Mobile Dock doesn't seem to support that feature and would go black screen instead. Ultrawide mode on the 1S however will work on devices that doesn't need the dock, like my laptop for example, but when using the dock to connect to my computer via HDMI and enabling ultrawide the screen goes black. Disappointed for sure, but perhaps Viture can release a firmware update to allow the dock to push ultrawide resolutions. Some day perhaps...I was looking at these compare to RayNeo Joydock and Xreal's Neo (I know confusing isn't it, the Neo doesn't belong to RayNeo but Xreal), but after much deliberation I found Viture's pro mobile dock to be the most complete for about the same price as the competition. What's got me the most sold though is how there's option for two glasses output as well as output for HDMI! So not only can you use this as a mobile dock, but also as a classic stationary dock to a tv. My only complaint and missed opportunity from Viture about this device is how you cannot connect charge the device while it's in use since the port that is used to charge it is the same as the port that's used to connect to the source device, meaning to connect to the Switch or Switch 2, etc. So in other words there's a limit to how long you can use these battery dependent, which I think to most people should be okay but for those diehards that wants to do a longer playthrough will need to force stop themselves to allow the device to charge before being to use it again. I haven't tried to test how long it'll take to drain the battery but my guess after my initial use suggests somewhere between 5-7 hours of play. Again, unfortunate how you can't use the dock and charge it, but I suppose it's okay and perhaps keeps costs down? Or so I hope that's the case.I still give it 5 stars because it works with my RayNeo Air 3S and should work with any device and isn't proprietary. I don't know if the other docks from RayNeo and Xreal are like either, but only on Viture's pro mobile dock here does it say on their product description that it works with "any" display-alt devices /glasses which is a welcome considering Nintendo's anti-consumerism take on their USB-C. Anyway, I digress. About the pro mobile dock, there doesn't seem to be any sort of lag or latency, or at least it's not noticeable to my eyes. It's also easy to use and is straightforward, just make the connections and you're good to go.A side note, I also have the attachment accessory for the switch 2 and they connect to one another perfectly. The plastics feels good and durable. At the time of this writing, the attachment kit had a promo that came free when you purchase this mobile dock, making this purchase an even better deal. I however mostly keep a protective case on my switch 2 which is not compatible with the attachment accessory, meaning if I can want to use the attachment accessory to connect the mobile dock to the switch 2, I first must remove the switch 2's protective case then can install the attachment.Overall this pro mobile dock from Viture to me is the superior dock accessory for your AR glasses thanks to its two output and HDMI output option, highly recommended!

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: **How was the item? VITURE Pro Mobile Dock** GARBAGE
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: **How was the item? VITURE Pro Mobile Dock**I purchased the VITURE Pro Mobile Dock because every review, influencer, sponsored video, and marketing page seemed determined to convince me that this was the magical device that would solve all my connectivity problems.Instead, it introduced entirely new ones.The primary feature of a dock is remarkably simple: take a signal from one device and pass it to another device without turning the image into modern art. Somehow, this dock struggles with that basic concept.Every device I connected through it looked like someone had accidentally deleted the color blue from existence. The image was drenched in red tones, making everything look like it was taking place during the apocalypse, on Mars, or inside a poorly lit nightclub. Skin tones were horrifying. White screens looked pink. Blue objects apparently offended the dock on a personal level and were removed from the viewing experience entirely.At first, I assumed I had a bad cable.Then I assumed I had a bad setting.Then I assumed I was doing something wrong.Eventually I realized the dock itself was the problem.What makes this even more frustrating is the marketing. The product is advertised as being broadly compatible with all sorts of devices. In practice, it feels like it was designed with one goal in mind: work with VITURE products and make everything else feel unwelcome.The compatibility claims remind me of restaurants that advertise "world-famous cuisine" because technically someone from another country once ate there.Can you get it working? Maybe.Should you have to spend hours troubleshooting a premium-priced dock whose entire job is passing through a video signal? Absolutely not.The best part is that while I was trying to diagnose the issue, I kept convincing myself there had to be some hidden setting, secret firmware update, or obscure cable combination that would magically fix everything. That's how these products get you. They transform customers into unpaid quality assurance engineers.By the end of the process, I wasn't using a dock. I was conducting a forensic investigation.**Pros*** Nicely packaged* Small form factor* Excellent at demonstrating various shades of red**Cons*** Severe color issues* Missing or distorted color channels* Compatibility claims feel wildly optimistic* Troubleshooting required for basic functionality* Expensive for what it delivers* Feels designed primarily for the manufacturer's own ecosystem* Turns simple setups into multi-hour projects**Final Verdict**The VITURE Pro Mobile Dock is the first dock I've ever owned that made me question whether colors are optional.I bought it expecting a plug-and-play accessory. What I received was a tiny red-tinted monument to disappointment. If your goal is to spend an evening wondering why everything looks like a scene from a post-apocalyptic movie, this dock performs flawlessly.Otherwise, save your money.A dock's job is to get out of the way and pass the signal through unchanged. This one apparently felt the need to express its artistic vision first.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Many DHCP video errors, codecs not supported, audio doesn't play; Terrible with a Roku Stick
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I was excited to finally jump into the XR glasses world, but the tech is incredibly finicky and picky about what it actually lets you play.After discovering neither my phone, tablet, or laptop worked completely with Viture Pro XR glasses, I had to get this Pro Dock as a final desperate measure. I used it with the glasses and a Roku Stick. In addition to the Dock I had to buy a MicroUSB-to-USBC cable to power the Stick with the Dock.The setup works, you can stream movies to the Roku Stick from your wireless router to watch with the glasses. However, it's incredibly picky about what it lets you play.-There's no sound from the glasses when using the Roku Media Player to play music. You can play the song, but there's no sound from the speakers.-You can hear the Roku Stick's start-up tone through the glasses. Great, I guess.-I can't play like 98% of my video files because of constant DHCP errors, unsupported video codecs, videos not compressed the way the Glasses/Dock likes them, etc. Seriously, you can't even watch free Roku TV, you get a DHCP error, so if we can't even watch stuff we're given permission to watch, how the heck are we supposed use these?-I found one video file I could play without issues; a grainy old .AVI video format episode of the Claymore anime I downloaded from somewhere over a decade ago. Are you kidding me? It will play this but it won't play the free stuff officially offered by Roku?I tried so hard to find an excuse to like the Viture Pro glasses, but the compatibility issues with this tech are suffocating. Make absolutely sure your file types and devices are compatible before ordering any of this stuff.Viture customer service did try to be helpful, so thanks for that.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Crib Mobile That is So Cute and It Comes with So Many Features
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This Baby Crib Mobile by LZZAPJ is so cute!  I ordered the one for boys (although girls could have it too.)This mobile starts with 4 little stuffed animals - a gray elephant, a yellow giraffe with silver spots, an orange and brown lion and one white and black one that AI and I can't identify. It's cute though.  Each one of them has a happy face which I like. The animals are all very well sewn and oh so soft. It also comes with  four 7.5 inch green leaves made out of stiff, good quality felt.I wish I had this all those years I took in children. This one has everything.  First, it rotates, that helps focusing development, It has music which helps soothe the child, and it has a projection to show stars. This whole mobile was designed to soothe the baby and help him sleep.It took me about an hour to put it together. Truthfully, probably 30 minutes of that hour was searching for AA batteries.  The batteries are not included. I think that was the only drawback to this mobile.  I did not deduct a star because I think I have just been so spoiled this last year with most items I received included everything I would need to use the product.They used  higher quality plastic on this.  However, once the child can pull on the animals, I would check this mobile weekly for stress on plastic and animals.  I would recommend this for up to one year old just from experience where children are stronger than we all think. They could also use this to stand up which could cause falls. You know your child. If he is trying to crawl or sitting up in his crib, it is time to take the mobile down.  Other than that, this is quality made with safety and functionI think the monetary value is right where it needs to be.This would make a thoughtful gift for Grandma or Grandpa's house crib, or  to new parents
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on August 11, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Cute Jungle Mobile with Lots of Music and a Handy Remote
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This baby mobile is adorable! I love the little jungle animals -the lion, elephant, giraffe, and the felt jungle leaves create such a sweet theme that would look great in any nursery.I did run into one issue during setup. The mobile takes 2 AA batteries, and the remote requires 2 AAA batteries. After installing the batteries, I couldn't get the mobile to turn on. After some trial and error, I discovered that the power switch on my unit only worked when positioned between the "On" and "Off" settings. Once I found that sweet spot, everything worked fine, but it definitely seemed a bit finicky. That's the reason I'm deducting one star.The music selection is extensive, with lots of songs to choose from. Most of the melodies are very pleasant, although a couple stood out to me as a little unusual. One tune has some odd clashing notes, and a few songs include electronic cymbal-like sounds that interrupted the melody more than I found soothing. That said, babies may respond differently, and there are PLENTY of other songs that are soft and enjoyable -some I would enjoy listening to!The projector is a nice feature, casting moon and star shapes onto the ceiling or wall while slowly changing colors. I also really appreciate the included remote. It lets you turn the mobile on and off, adjust the volume, control the rotating mobile, and operate the projector without having to walk over to the crib. That's especially helpful if you've just gotten your little one to sleep.This is a cute, feature-packed baby mobile with lots of music options, a fun projector, and the convenience of a remote. I'm giving it 4 stars because of the finicky power switch on my unit, but otherwise it's been a nice addition to the nursery.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on August 6, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I do not think I have seen a mobile have quite so many cool features. You cant go wrong with a cute jungle theme. It is a very gender neutral design aesthetic. It is super easy to attach and once it is attached you get to start exploring all of the really cool things it can do. It is a mobile so of course it rotates. It has music and not just one or 2 songs but so many different ones in such a wide variety of styles. You can then play those songs with a very big varying degree of loudness for super soft to being able to hear it in the other room clearly. But that is not all, you then have a projector that puts on a beautiful light show above babies crib. I mean this thing is fully loaded. Right now it is priced at $29 and if you compare it to other $29 mobiles, they do not have all the wonderful things this one does. So this, I would say is a great deal.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: My sister’s baby shower was coming up and I needed something that wouldn't end up in a junk drawer two weeks later. This Baby Crib Mobile with Remote is pretty straightforward, which is exactly what I was looking for. I am relieved it was straightforward to put together because I usually hate messing with plastic clamps and tiny screws. It fits onto the slats without sliding around, which is a big relief. The plush animals like the lion and giraffe are soft enough for a kid to grab, and you can actually take them off if they want to play with them separately. The star projector adds some color to the ceiling, which keeps the kid occupied for a bit. Using the remote is a nice touch because you don't have to tip-toe over and risk waking them up just to turn the music down. It takes a few different batteries that aren't included, which was a bit of a headache to hunt down in my kitchen drawer. The volume has a few settings, and luckily it gets quiet enough that it doesn't drive the parents crazy in the next room. It does the job without being overly complicated. Just make sure you have a screwdriver handy for the battery cover.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I like how this mobile has soft toys rather than hard ones like many other mobiles have. The clamp does not work with a fabric bassinet, though. The projector light only seems to have one level and it isn't very bright. My kids are older, so we are using it as a hanging, spinning music box with a projector light of stars, but you need to have it in very short distance in order for the stars to show. The music is soft and easy to listen to, it is relaxing even for me, so I don't mind having it on at night. It apparently has a timer that shuts it off, do I've been having to turn it back on until I tinker with the clock button. What I don't like is the front of the mobile only has a sticker instead of maybe some lights or something for baby to look at when it is obviously dark enough to turn the mobile on. The sticker isn't much to look at in the dark.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Didnt we ditch console TVs for this?
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This is the perfect unselfish TV stand - if you are not interested in a piece of furniture that gobbles up space and forces you to put "stuff" on it to make it worth the space it is taking up, then you need this TV stand. It does its job, nothing more and nothing less - it holds up the TV. I replaced a giant and expensive TV stand for this because I was tired of dusting it and being unable to move it around. This stand was about a quarter of the price and is a perfect fit in my life. It came within 12 hours. It took about 30 minutes to put together including mounting the TV, its super-sturdy yet completely mobile. There is a small shelf that you can mount or leave off - it is just big enough for a game console (or dvd player if you are still using one).What you dont get (that could be a deal breaker for you) - you dont get any kind of "cord winder" or "cord keeper" to organize any cords from the TV, cables/streaming boxes, etc. I wish that it would have at least come with some velco straps to tie everything down - but I still love it. You also dont get fashion - this is all utility but its so minimal that it would fit most anywhere.I finally have space back in my room. It will be easy to clean and move to clean behind. And I can now move the TV anywhere in the room with little disruption. If you are looking for a high quality, sturdy TV stand - this is the RIGHT STAND and the RIGHT PRICE. Highly Recommend!

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: It is what they say it is, and it works as described and well.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I don't write a lot of reviews. Most things are either "blah...it is what it is and nothing special" or "it was a PITA and I returned it or it just wasn't right.This one, though...it IS what they say it is AND it actually was much better, and easier to put together, than I thought when I made the purchase.So, back story.....I have an "extra 55in TV" since it just got repaired and I had gotten a replacement in the meantime.  I also have a "games room" with a full size craps table, seating, dart board, etc.  I wanted to mount the TV but, due to windows in that room, the only place I could mount it on the wall would actually be on the fireplace.  I hesitated doing that.  So, I searched for portable TV stands.  I had looked, years ago, for similar, and didn't like what I saw.This time, I looked at a few dozen.  I read the reviews (filtering out the BS ones, imo) and read the questions (people!  Read product descriptions before asking questions!  I saw a lot of questions that were answered either in the product title or immediate description).After a few hours of research, I went back to one of the first 2 I had initially looked at, and this was the one I chose.It arrived and, as I am having some problems with my leg, I can't knee or squat down or do other things that would have made putting it together much easier, but, that said, I was still able to do it, on my own.Just took a little longer, but still didn't take too long. Probably 30 minutes.When putting together, unpack everything, place on table (in my case) or floor, and have the instructions out.  Follow the instructions. Nothing tricky. They are actually pretty easily written in English and the photos are easy to follow as well.  Don't get ahead of yourself and just doublecheck your steps as you go.They give you all the tools you need (until the end when you do need a small philips head screwdriver to secure the mount in the last step).  All the parts are there, and segmented appropriately, in the packaging...and labeled well....instead of a mishmash of parts where you have to separate them on your own.The TV I mounted was a Samsung 55" LCD and I was able to mount it on my own (I'm 5'10" and not weak, but I feel that most males around my size and many females that are 5'6" or more, and are ok lifting 30-40 pounds on their own can do this.  Wingspan has more to do with this than lifting weights for this. If in doubt, get a friend. Most 2 person groups could lift and mount super easily, I believe).I've had it installed and in use all afternoon and this evening now, as I put it next to my craps table and I have been shooting dice with it on.  I enjoy having my TV in the same room instead of just hearing it from another room....and, when the weather gets nice again, with this mount, we can always wheel it out on the deck and watch TV in the evening while enjoying the outdoors.The one thing that I wish were a little different is the tray.  What they have done is functional and no complaints.  I just wish there were an easy way to have the tray on the back of the unit as I don't like stuff distracting my view when I am watching TV (that's on me for letting it distract me).  I do understand that, for some, that wouldn't work to have it on the backside as it may, depending on what is put there, unbalance the unit and cause a tipping hazard though.Overall, for the price paid, this is pretty darn good.  Does not feel cheap or shoddy at all. Feels well constructed and quality parts.  Good job on making this!

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Cute pack n play mobile, but has some flaws.Cute pack n play mobile, but has some flaws.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I was looking for a mobile to attach to our Graco Pack n Play Close to Baby Bassinet version and found that this item really doesn't exist. It's mostly mobiles that attach to cribs/vertical rails. So I bought this one in hopes for the best based on the mixed reviews.Pros:- Has several features (a couple are useless - see cons) that are nice like rotation, night light, and light show- Easy to assemble- Rotation is whisper quiet, you can only hear it when right next to it- Looks nice even though it's all cheap plastic- Has an automatic off for the rotation function- Can easily change out the animals if you'd like- Mobile/base can swivel for placement/adjustmentCons:- Two features are absolutely useless (vibrate & music) and I would have preferred those buttons be used for more options like having the light show be it's own button and not automatically on when rotation is on. Vibration mode feels like those old coin operated vibrating beds at cheap motels. There's no reason to vibrate your crib/pack n play.- Music is too loud even on lowest volume. The decibel reading is 55-60+ dB on the quietest setting which can hurt baby's hearing when exposed for prolonged times.- Night light is a cool white and should have been a warm white- You have to cycle through volume and brightness by pressing the same button. Would have been better if there was a separate + or - buttons that controlled those functions instead.- There's no adjustable width on the base. Most reviewers are able to put a washcloth underneath to fit their pack n play models, which doesn't feel secure/safe to me. But for my model, the clips that hold the bassinet get in the way as well as the buttons on the wides to disassemble, so I was almost unable to use it altogether until I found a small spot that barely works right underneath the changing table. There should be some kind of adjustable screw or grip to secure this better.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: Als Gundam Fan finde ich das F91 als einer der besten eigenständigen Filme des Gundam Universums gilt.Und das ohne bekannte Charaktere aufzuweisen.Wirft man einen Blick auf die Rückseite der DVD, hält man sich vielleicht mit dem mal wieder ( ungewollt ? ) lustigen Vornamen des Hauptcharakters auf, nur um sich sekunden später beim Start des Films in einen fantastisch inszenierten Auftakt eines neuen Konflikts der Zeitrechnung "Universal Century" wiederzufinden. Und das Jahre nach den Ereignissen von " Char's Counterattack " welcher ja auch in Deutschland wenigstens auf DVD erhältlich ist.Gut hierbei ist, das man kein Experte sein muss, selbst wer noch keinen Gundam Film gesehen hat wird nicht mit Details oder Rückblenden überhäuft oder wirklich fragend in seinem Heimkino sitzen müssen.Hommagen an frühere Serien, oder gar Star Wars wurden dezent wie eine kleine Prise Salz eingestreut und sollten keinen üblen Nachgeschmack verursachen, sondern eher hier und da ein Grinsen hervorbringen.Im grossen und ganzen wirkt der Film eher ernster, und scheut sich auch nicht vor dem ein oder anderen tragischen Ereigniss.Genau das macht aber meiner Meinung nach die Qualität aus, wer einmal die ersten etwa 20 Folgen der Serie Gundam ZZ gesehen hat, weiss vielleicht was ich meine.Nichts ist Perfekt, und es gibt hier bei Gundam F91 auch paar Szenen die ich mir anders vorgestellt hätte, dennoch wars mal wieder ein Genuss.Bild und Tonqualität gehen für einen normale DVD völlig in Ordnung, der Umfang ist eben gering, aber das ist für rund 10 Euro ok.Vielleicht kommt er auch hierzulande ja mal als Blu-Ray heraus, hoffen darf man immer.Kurzum:Es wäre nicht schlecht gewesen, wäre F91 als ganze Serie oder zumindest Mehrteiler gekommen, aber Gundam-Fans würde ich ihn dennoch ans Herz legen, da zwar nichts neues, aber die bekannten Zutaten wohl proportioniert eingesetzt werden.Und die Nicht-Fans, welche aber gerne Science-Fiction auch als Anime sehen, sollten es sich mal ansehen , insbesondere wenn man nur mal einen " Blick " ins Gundam Universum werfen möchte, und das zum kleinen Preis.

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: Un exelente producto y llegó en tiempo forma

Oil filters are critical components in the operation of an internal combustion engine.  If an oil filter fails, it could cause very expensive engine failures that would cost thousands to repair. Even if it does not completely fail, a poor quality filter could cause significant harm to an engine over time.Today's engines are being designed to run on synthetic oil. Further, the manufacturers are recommending longer and longer drain intervals.  No longer is oil supposed to be changed after 3000miles (5000KM), many car companies are now recommending oil changes after 10,000 miles or greater.  True full synthetic oils are able to protect the engine over these greater distances if, and only if, they have the correct oil filter.After doing a lot of research, it is clear that it is not easy to know what oil filters are good and which ones are not.  There are so many brands in the market place.  The Mobil1 extended filter stands out from the crowd of filters.The filter is better built than most. All the components are just better quality. If you take it apart it is easy to see that there has been some thought put into the design and build.  But equally important, the filter is backed by Mobil and Champion (they build the filter for Mobil) and they guarantee your engine against oil filter caused damage for 20,000miles or one year.These are my first choice in oil filters for our Acura. The car has 200,000miles320,000KM and the engine is still in excellent condition.  Regular synthetic oil changes (7500miles) with Mobil1 filters work for our family car.  If the filter were to fail and cause a problem, good and reputable companies are going to be on the hook. The filters are more expensive then many, but when you do the research, not many oil filter products are guaranteed to last 20,000miles or even 10,000 miles; these are.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Got sick of paying Sprint (later T-Mobile) crazy monthly fees.  But wasn't excited about going through the conversion myself (without a store clerk/tech there to do it).  But I have to say, it wasn't bad at all!First, Mint is a T-Mobile sub-carrier, so I was reassured that I was not "going far" in my case.  (this doesn't really matter)Second, setting it up is easy.  You install the app on your phone and create an account.  You stick the chip into your phone.  You tell the app your chip number.  Hit a few more Next Next Next buttons, and boom, you're done.  The whole thing took about 5 minutes.I did 5 of these in one evening.  4 of them were done in 5 minutes.  1 of them took about 15-20 before the system picked that person up.  Not sure why, but who cares.  It works great for everyone, now.The price is fantastic.  Note that it's an introductory price.  It went up by about $5/month after the intro period was over.  But this is still WAY cheaper.Coverage is great... it's uses T-Mobile's network, so it's as good as their network is in your area.  Supposedly, as a sub-carrier, T-Mobile reserves the right to slow you down when things get congested, so their main customers can have priority.  If this has ever happened, I've never noticed.  I say, go for it.Bandwidth is 4 gb/month, which is fine for more users.  I use less than a gig per month because i'm always in wireless places.  The wife walks the dog on the trail and listens to podcasts & stuff, so she uses all of her 4 gb/month.  You can buy more, but it can get pricey, like $10 per extra gig.  If you don't buy it, your data use is slowed WAY down when you run out... technically it still works, but it will feel like the 56k modem days.  So decide if the 4 gb is enough for you.  There are 5 of us, and only 1 of us even comes close to using it all each month.The app isn't very detailed.  It's cute, modern, even a little edgy in style.  But it didn't NOT give you detail on your bandwidth.  It will tell you your total, and dates when it will replenish, but that's about it.  Probably good enough for 90% of the people out there.  I would like to know more about what apps or types of data I'm burning through, but I suppose you can get a lot of that off your phone if it's at all modern.I'm loving Mint, and highly recommend it.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on October 26, 2022

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I honestly hadn't given T-Mobile's network a shot since 2002 when I bought my Nokia 3650. It wasn't great back then...not was it years before when it was Voicestream. I have been with Verizon since 2003 and hadn't ever looked back regardless of my bills skyrocketing with grandfathered unlimited data and hotspot ($50/mo per line for data, $30 for hotspot, $70 for 1400 shared minutes, $30 for unlimited family texting plus $9.99 for each line to access the minutes and texting). My bills were north of $375/mo every month by the time I added one phone installment of $25/mo and insurance. I paid this for a LONG time knowing that if I changed plans I wouldn't be able to get my unlimited data and hotspot back. For 8+ years of this time I worked for AT&T and their terrible network and lack of unlimited plans never once lured me away from Big Red...even though I would have gotten half off as an employee.Regardless...my needs changed, I'm not travelling as much as I figured there was no point in paying that high bill when I used an average of 4gb of data per month now. In an ironic twist I moved somewhere with no Verizon signal on my property and only AT&T worked there. But I still couldn't get signal inside with team Blue...only if I went outdoors. I found out that their features such as WiFi calling only work with AT&T branded devices but I have been a Nexus/Pixel guy for years and wasn't about to change to an (in my opinion) inferior Samsung or Apple device just to use wifi calling.So I did my research, found that T-Mobile had poured a lot of money into low band spectrum that penetrates buildings better and travels further. So I looked into MVNOs like Mint and found MANY options, but the best for the price was Mint. I ordered a sim card to test out the service...and everything worked perfectly on my Pixel 2 XL. Wifi calling, visual voicemail with transcription, RCS messaging, etc. Granted, they still had no signal on my property so I instead put up a high gain omnidirectional WiFi access point on a pole outside my house and it covered all 3 acres without a hitch.So now I'm paying $35/mo for 8GB of data with unlimited talk and text that works in 95% of the places my Verizon worked at. PLUS I'm able to use all of the features of my phone that AT&T wouldn't support simply because they want to trap everyone into a 24-30 month installment plan on a new phone.Remember when we used to pay $200 for a top of the line phone with a 2 year contract and our cell bills were lower too? Well, I do. Carriers would subsidize the price and we would agree to pay for a while. Now we all pay $1000 for the phone and somehow our bills are astronomically higher than they used to be despite the fact that we talk less, text more, and use data most. They were more than happy to give me an 'aircard' with unlimited data back in 2009, but somehow it's not possible now in 2019 with more efficient networks and MUCH more spectrum than they've ever had access to? Gotta love that capitalism.Anyway, if you haven't given the magenta network a try in a while, try it again. It's made major strides. It's also the only network in the US that doesn't restrict features simply because you brought your own device. Maybe if enough of us make the switch to these smaller MVNOs the big MNOs will take notice and start treating customers better.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on November 27, 2019

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: You need to activate it within 45 days! Otherwise very happy with it so far.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: (UPDATE: I liked this 3 months SIM so much that I purchased a 6 month SIM direct from Mint. I didn't need to use it right away so I just stuck it in a drawer. A month later I got an email from Mint warning me that if I didn't activate the SIM within 45 days from purchase, it would be permanently deactivated! There was nothing on their website mentioning this. I contacted their support and was told that this policy comes from T-Mobile (Mint uses their network) and actually the SIM might still activate after 45 days. But if it didn’t, I could contact Mint support and they would get it working - though it could take 5-7 business days. This definitely is something that they should make clear in their product info. I’m also not sure about blaming it on T-Mobile since I know that US Mobile - which also uses the T-Mo network - has SIM cards that last 2 years before needing to be activated. The rest of this review is about the 3 month card I purchased from Amazon, before I got the 6 month card.)Overall I’m really happy with Mint so far. It was easy to set up, the service works well, and support is good too.Activating the card was seamless, the info provided with the SIM and on their website was really well organized and clear and the process was easy. You can choose to add a credit card for auto-renew when the 3 months are up, but I skipped that. About the minor negative I noticed during activation is that I didn’t get to choose my new number from a list; instead they just assigned me one. Once activation was finished the website clearly told me how to update my phone’s data settings (though I found that on my phone, the first few steps were a bit different though it wasn’t hard to figure out).Mint uses T-Mobile’s network so signal strength and call quality and data speed are all fine on my Moto E4 phone. Voicemail and international texting is included (I tried both). International calling is available too, but only if you first add credit to your account - however even though I never added any credit, I could still make International calls (at least short ones - I haven’t tried more than that). Voice and texts are unlimited and so is data, though after you’ve used 2GB data, it’s supposed to slow down (a lot) until the start of the next monthly cycle. But as with the international calling glitch, I found that even once I had used up my 2GB (which I confirmed by checking my account on their website), my LTE data speed was not noticeably any slower than before.Since I was concerned that allowing me to make International calls without me paying in advance could come back to bite me later, I contacted their support via email. I got a reply within a few hours assuring me that they would investigate and I wouldn’t be charged. Similarly when I noticed that data wasn’t slowing down after 2GB was used up, I sent another email, the equally quick reply told me they would look into that too. Since neither of these are really problems (who doesn’t want free int’l calling or free unlimited high speed data?), it doesn’t bother me that both issues seem to still be happening a week later - but it is a bit concerning that if they give away stuff they’re supposed to be charging for, that might not bode well for their long term business success!P.S. If you get this card for a friend/family member and activate it for them, the good news is that although during activation you need to provide an email and a name and password, later on the only info needed to log in is the phone number and password (and once logged in you can change any of that other info including the password).Also P.S. The number I got must have been recycled. Every few days I get a robocall from the same company asking me to call back about an overdue payment.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This is a sweet and cute mobile. The music is pretty and sounds nice. The nature sound and heartbeat sound are a little less crisp but still fine. The mobile itself rotates well, plays music and lights up well. I cannot get the projector image to show correctly though- half of it is not in focus and is blurry… not that a bay will see that far away immediately anyway but still noteworthy. Hopefully mine is just a fluke. I’m not sure that this one is THE most visually stimulating, but it’s still cute and creates movement etc. The real MVP though is the remote! This is my favorite feature- it allows me to turn on the mobile without baby seeing me and fussing to be picked up. You can control just about everything with the remote and it’s so helpful! I also really like that the animals turn into rattles to be played with later. It makes something that is only for a small season, useful for a bit longer. I wish I had this one for my first two! Overall I think this Mobil is great and would recommend it.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great phone in this price range
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This verges on top-of-the-line when it comes to *affordable* phones. It has better specs in every important way than the Moto G 2025, and is about equivalent in important ways to phones that cost twice as much. It's about the same form factor and style as its ancestor, the Moto 5G Ace from a couple of years ago (my prior phone). Getting it here instead of from your provider's store means you have less annoying bloatware installed, and it may even be cheaper too.I'm satisfied with the G Power's speed, storage and memory, ease of use, camera quality (vastly better than the Ace!), all of it. The adjustability for people without great vision is a plus (for me anyway). I really don't have anything to complain about with this phone. I tried the Moto G 2025 (the "little sibling" of this Moto G Power), and it just didn't have the capacity I wanted (I'm a bit of an app and media hoarder). I tried to get the Moto G Power from Metro, but their store staff said there were none avialable from them any longer in the entire area, so I ordered it here instead.The data backup (from old phone) and restore (to new phone), including all apps, appears to have worked flawlessly. I did not lose apps, or contacts, or media. Various apps did have to be reconfigured on first-run on the new phone, but I expected that. Using Nova Launcher, it even restored all my app groups/folders, and every icon to its original position. Nice. It's like having the same phone expect better than it was before.This phone coming with Android 15 out of the box is great (compared to phones still on sale today that have Android 14 or even 13). For me anyway, it did 3 system updates in as many days, so it's staying current (withing the Android 15 channel). My reason for upgrading to this phone at this time was that the Ace phone being stuck at an older Android version was a problem for me (e.g. one of my e-banking apps refused to work on the old OS any longer). I don't know if this phone will be upgradable to Android 16 (which has already been out for 3 months as of this writing), or what that upgrade process might be.A heads-up with regard to Metro by T-Mobile: If you try to have them set this phone up for you in the store, they are likely to claim that you have to get a different and more expensive plan than the one you have, claiming this phone "isn't compatible" with your current plan. This is nonsense. Instead, try to change your phone to this one using the website. If it doesn't work, use an old or borrowed phone to call Metro's customer service and talk to a real person through that system, and have them enable the new phone for you (either with an e-SIM or by moving your existing SIM card from original phone to new one), and make it clear that you expect to keep your original number and keep your existing plan (or have an equivalent one with same price for same level of service). If necessary, they can have a supervisor override any roadblocks. This step may be especially important for anyone qualifying for discounted service due to being on disability, social security, etc.  While I'm going on my experience with Metro, similar caveats may apply to other carriers. They're all being more aggressive about trying to wedge more money out of people without actually improving their service level. Don't let them do that to you just because you got this particular phone (and didn't get it from them).Another caveat: Phones like this are fragile, unfortunately. You absolutely do need a protective case, not just a screen protector (that protects against scratches, not drops and other impacts). I would say order the case and screen protector before the phone, or at least to arrive on same day. You do not want to be tempted to carry this phone around and use it without the case being put on yet.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I am really happy with this phone. It's fast, it has a bright and decent crisp display. It was a replacement for an LG V20 which was a premium phone in its day. This phone is considered a budget phone, but is superior to the V20 in so many ways, mainly because the industry has advanced so much in 10 years.Negatives are the taller skinnier profile is slightly harder to read than my old phone. I think this is typical of newer phones. The sound quality is good, but it lacks multichannel recording software that was native to my V20. The camera is adequate, nothing extraordinary.Definite pluses are long battery life and built in headphone jack. No issues setting it up. After transferring the data off my old phone using the built in software, I just moved my Verizon SIM (it's unlocked);and my SD card into the built-in tray on the side. No need to pay Verizon $35 to set it up. There are biometric security features that I don't use, but they are good if you like them.I got the phone for $13 using credit card points (list was like $139) so it was a super deal for me. No regrets, great for normal everyday use or as a bridge phone when your $1000+ Samsung phone fails.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: 04/25/2026 updateI'm raising this back to 5 stars ... faulty charging Moto wire and power brick wasn't the phone at all ... tested with other devices and had bad results as well, so I threw out the original Moto wire and power brick.========================================================================================03/16/2026 updateI'm taking off a star from my review.  Something strange is happening with charging the phone. Suddenly it started locking up to 30% and requires a restart for it to go forward. Nothing specific happened, no system updates, and I'm going to keep my eye on it for now since I can't troubleshoot to anything.=========================================================================================I took a chance and ordered this phone from Amazon Resale and received a very generous discount off the discounted price.  Hopefully I didn't just buy someone else's problem.  For starters, the box I received it in was shabby and dirty and the charging cable was unraveled  in the box, however the phone was wrapped in plastic and appears intact with a fully charged battery. I am a big fan of Motorola and this is my fourth phone from them. While my most recent Edge 2021 5g is still in perfect working condition, I just couldn't pass up this Motorola G Power 2025 at this ridiculously low holiday sales price especially given the impressive technical specs that it comes with.  I did read many of the reviews both good and especially the bad ones to see if there is a pattern of something inherently wrong with this model. I couldn't tell since some of the reviews are very sparse on actual details. So here goes my review for the "Moto G Power - 2025, UNLOCKED, Made for US 8-128gb, 50MP Camera":Cons:I'm doing this first since it's important that you understand what you're getting into with this phone.-The phone is slightly smaller (length), slightly thicker and slightly heavier than my Edge 2021 5g - not a big deal but worth noting-The phone comes with standard factory load like all phones but for a 2025 model this appears to beinadequate as I will explain in the next bullet point-The phone is a quick boot and once up and running it will immediately pair with your previous phone (if you allow it) and begin transferring data and configurations along with any Google backups you may have.  This is where things get choppy - there isn't an obvious way to select what to transfer and in not providing a screen pause with choices it embarks on downloading your entire library of photos, videos and music which for many of us may be a long and exhausting process that may quickly fill up the phone 128gb.  In doing so it also begins to initiate Updates to the phone OS thereby doing double duty and an extremely lengthy process where it also shuts down your screen (power saver) and causing you to periodically have to sign back in, which in turn pauses the Updates and you have to restart them.  This is both frustrating and ill conceived by the manufacturer. I actually decided to stop it, reset to factory setting and restart without any account and data restoration just so I can process the phone OS Updates.-The phone OS Updates take "several hours" (that's right "several") and if you don't monitor them they will stop (all are required and all are sequential) making this a multi-hour project.  If you don't monitor and apply each one, then the Updates stop and will Update and Restart at what it thinks are your off-hours. This explains why so many reviews keep complaining about the phone being slow, not having proper connectivity, randomly rebooting, etc. etc. All those things are accurate and true if the phone is left to its own "smart" schedule for OS Updates and would frustrate you for days or possibly weeks, by my estimate, even if you are a techie but make some reasonable assumptions around the data transfer and phone OS Updates which in fact are not how it works at all on this phone.Pros:-The phone was actually less expensive then the Edge 2021 5g which I also bought on an Amazon sales event, even though the new Mediatek chip and RAM are much, much, much better than my Edge 2021 - storage is the same - 128gb.-The phone is solid and well built end to end - "stunningly impressive" are also its IP67/IP68/MIL-STD 810H ratings which no other phone that I am aware of can make claim to at this price point. A heavy duty phone without a heavy price.-It boots quickly, the screen is absolutely gorgeous and extremely crisp and clear in all light conditions.-The phone overall is very, very, very fast with the Meadiatek chip and RAM.  In fact this is the fastest phone I've ever had.-Plenty of storage at 128gb for average user and I added a 1TB SDHC which went in quickly and works better than any other SDHC on any other phone I've ever had.- Battery is tremendously well tuned with the phone and with a 36% screen setting, which is perfect for me visually, I can use this phone heavily for nearly 52 hrs - above and beyond what the manufacturer rates it-The speakers on the phone are also exceptionally good and pleasant to use without sounding echoey and whinny - won't replace your high end audio devices but pretty good as is and plenty loud.-The rear camera absolutely shines at 50mp and takes very impressive pictures in all light conditions and all settings macro/.5/1x/2x - the front camera is also OK for most uses and selfies.  Some people commented on getting terrible pictures and I'm not sure how or why, but it may be caused by lack of understanding on how to Tune your camera under Settings to meet your use expectations, or how to switch camera modes on the bottom front screen when using the camera.  Either way I think this is miles above my Edge 2021 5g.-WiFi/5g is blazing fast and I can watch any of my video or play any game without the phone chocking, stopping or buffering.-Voice connectivity is excellent and I haven't experienced any problems at all as described by some of the other reviews.  I tested the phone recently across 3 US states in the NorthEast on a 450 mile round trip and had zero problems at all while playing music, using Google Maps, responding to text via voice connectivity and initiating or receiving phone calls.-Charges very, very fast with a 30W brick and corresponding USB-C wire AND even more impressive it has WIRELESS charging ability with a 15W pad which is also very fast and convenient especially at office or overnight by bedside - a rare feature at this price point-Last but not least - once you get through all the phone OS Updates you wind up with the latest and greatest Motorola Android 16 version which is spectacular.  Can't ask for anything more if you can endure the pain of the OS setup which is no small feat for most users.Additional note:-Some negative reviews note that the phone doesn't work with their specific providers, or has problems when you swap your SIM. My suggestion is that you should immediately check your new IMEI with your provider for compatibility before you start to do any work on the new phone, and MOST IMPORTANTLY, request a new SIM or eSIM for your new phone.  Rarely does swapping an old SIM that was provisioned for your old phone IMEI work well, or at all, in a new phone.  This is a security and safety feature for most wireless providers.I highly recommend this phone.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Gets the job done, won't blow your socks off
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: My old phone, a Samsung Galaxy S10, no longer seemed to be able to connect to network data anymore, and I did everything except factory reset to try to fix it because I have too much on it I don't want to erase and backing it all up is too difficult (some apps are out of date and no longer supported, etc) especially without knowing for sure that a FR would work.So, I bought this phone as a sort of last ditch solution.  Honestly, it's better than I expected.  Nice screen size.  Looks decent.  Has all the capabilities I need on a daily basis.  However, I will say this: there are lots of elements of this phone, despite it being four years newer than my Galaxy S10, that are below the S10's specs: screen resolution is a big one, as is processor speed and RAM. Superficially is the exterior which, unlike the Samsung, doesn't have tempered glass, but I actually kind of like the exterior of this slightly better even if it does look less "premium" because the S10's glass on the backside of the phone just smudges and scratches.  Also, the phone is about 6.7oz or so, so it's heavier than the S10 by about a half oz.In terms of the other elements of comparison I noted: RAM is 4gigs vs the Galaxy's 8 gigs, and the Qualcomm Snapdragon 4 Gen 1 is definitely a more budget processor vs the Galaxy S10's processor specs.  The biggest though is the screen resolution at 1612x720 vs the Galaxy's 1440x3040.  The PPI (pixel density) is essentially half that of my old phone, so I definitely notice that in watching videos, and I'm sure you will too if you're going from a more "premium" brand.The good?  The camera at 50mp vs the Galaxy's 10mp, the battery at 50mAh which is bigger (but no wireless charging), the screen size, the exterior styling which I actually like, and of course the elephant in the room which is price.Is this a good deal for the price?  Absolutely.  I will be keeping mine.  Though the specs aren't as good in critical areas vs my old phone, nothing beats owning your phone outright at only $150 and not having to be tethered to a network or make payments.  So is it worth it?  Absolutely.  Just don't expect it to perform at the levels of any "premium" brand in terms of multitasking or expect the same kind of beautiful granularity on videos.  It's a budget phone, after all, so expect some compromises, but it gets the job done and again, the price is only about 1.5x the *monthly* cost of buying a premium phone from Verizon etc.  So literally, after about 2 months it's basically paid for itself vs buying a "premium" brand phone direct from the big networks.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Moto G Power 5G 2024Received new unlocked phone, put my Boost Mobile sim in turned it on and used the included usb cable to transfer the files and settings over from my previous phone, a Moto G Fast from 2021.  (I did not have contacts, photos, etc. backed up to the cloud) It works good.  Had it 5 days and so far it is great for the price.  Update: Now just skip to the end.My ringtone assignments were not transferred from the old phone - all using the default.  I had to go manually add mp3's as ringtones and assign them to individuals.  Also my alarms the same thing.  It upgraded to Android 15 and I'm not sure how I like some things about Android 15 compared to the Android 11 that I was using previously.  Eventually Android will be more bloated and full of idiotic (dis)improvements that hamper you than Windows if it isn't already.I really like the Moto Gestures but not a fan of the power button being reconfigured by default.  The camera seems ok but no better than the 4 year old one with many less megapixels.  Didn't notice anything new in the camera software or photo editor from the 4 year older one.  Not sure but I think that I took some pictures that were verified with the shutter sound but then no pictures were in the album.  I am saving camera pics to the micro sd card.  I will keep an eye on this to see if its an actual issue.  No charger/power plug is included.  No USB A to USB C cable is included.  A USB C to USB C cable is included.  Good for phone to phone transfer or if you have a USB C female plug or PC/Tablet with USB C port.  So I am using my 4 year old charger and cable even though I don't think its rated for as quick of charging as the new phone.  I may have to get a 30W charger plug and cable or 15W charging pad.Its been a few months now.  The phone still works good.  As with all phones and connected devices now, the apps on it collect and send a lot of data on your wifi and using your bandwidth and data cap.  I've been using the Gemini AI that comes up when you press the power button.  Its hit or miss and you always have to know when to tell it its wrong and then it says "oh, you're right, I'm sorry".  It uses much, much more power so a charge that would last 2 days normally will last, literally, 3 or 4 hours of chatting with the Gemini AI about anything, useful or not.Google keeps insisting that I backup my photos and such to their cloud but I don't want to - its not secure and they haven't paid me to use my data for training their AI that they are using to make billions of dollars off of as they jettison more and more employees, bankrupting the whole system, so why should I give it away for free?  No, I just copy them to my PC instead, its much, much more private and secure.  No need for a secretive shady middle man making like Igor stealing people's corpses in the night LoL.  If Google wants data for training purposes we can discuss payment and usage terms.  Until then, greedy hands off!OK so the last time I used my phone I was met with a notification from Android that my age could not be verified and so it changed parental controls and other settings on my phone.  It did not give any other info. If I didn't like it, send a copy of my driver's license to prove my identity and age.  So it doesn't take a crystal ball to see the connection and know Google has treated me like a child and locked me out of my own phone based upon faulty AI output.  Is this the Twilight Zone?  I don't know but I'm not sending a copy of my license anywhere to fix Gemini Ai's mistake.  I am online ordering an iphone now and thought I'd also update this review to let people know about Android and Google's ability to change settings on your own devices based upon some faulty AI logic or glitches or hallucinations or whatever they choose to call it. productPageReviews.reviewDescription: The DJI Osmo Mobile SE Intelligent Gimbal is a game-changer for anyone seeking to up their mobile filmmaking and photography game. As a portable and foldable 3-axis phone gimbal, it offers an impressive array of features that make capturing smooth, professional-quality videos and photos easier than ever before.Right out of the box, the Osmo Mobile SE impresses with its sleek and compact design. Its foldable arms make it incredibly convenient to carry around, ensuring that you're always ready to capture life's spontaneous moments without the hassle of lugging around bulky equipment.The real magic of the Osmo Mobile SE, however, lies in its intelligent stabilization technology. The 3-axis gimbal system works tirelessly to eliminate shakes and jitters from your footage, resulting in silky-smooth videos that rival those of professional filmmakers. Whether you're recording a bustling cityscape or a dynamic action sequence, this gimbal ensures that your shots remain steady and captivating.Setting up the Osmo Mobile SE is a breeze, thanks to its user-friendly interface and intuitive controls. The accompanying mobile app provides an impressive range of shooting modes, from the basic follow and pan functions to more advanced options like time-lapse and motion control. The app's simple yet powerful editing tools further enhance your creative possibilities, allowing you to add cinematic flair to your content.One standout feature is the ActiveTrack technology, which enables the gimbal to automatically track and follow subjects as they move, ensuring that they remain centered and in focus throughout your recording. This is particularly handy for capturing dynamic scenes or creating vlogs where you're both the cameraperson and the subject.Battery life is commendable, providing ample shooting time to cover your creative endeavors. Additionally, the Osmo Mobile SE can also function as a portable charger for your smartphone, which is a thoughtful addition for those who often find themselves low on battery during extended shoots.In terms of build quality, DJI has upheld its reputation for crafting durable and reliable equipment. The gimbal feels sturdy in hand and can withstand the rigors of outdoor shoots. The phone clamp secures your device snugly, ensuring that it remains safe and stable throughout filming.In conclusion, the DJI Osmo Mobile SE Intelligent Gimbal is a must-have tool for content creators, vloggers, and aspiring filmmakers who want to capture professional-quality videos with ease. Its intelligent stabilization, user-friendly interface, and compact design make it a standout in the world of smartphone gimbals. Whether you're a beginner or a seasoned pro, the Osmo Mobile SE will undoubtedly elevate your mobile filmmaking experience to new heights.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Very cool and has lots of neat features, minor annoyancesVery cool and has lots of neat features, minor annoyances
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I really like this product, and it is really neat. I think it's a good deal for the price. One thing that's super cool is it stabilizes the phone for when you're moving, which is awesome. You can easily switch from landscape to vertical with just the push of a button. You can also turn the phone around with the push of a button and turn the camera. It's really useful and it's high quality.I like that it comes with an app, and the app has other cool features for filming with, like blurring effects and different cool filming effects. They teach you in the app how to do different cool shots and things. It's definitely really well made, and I like it a lot.The downsides are:• There isn't an easy way to turn the whole phone around. You can turn the camera, choose whether you want front-facing or back-facing camera very easily, but you just have to turn the whole gimbal if you want to turn the phone around because the actual joystick only goes right and left. It doesn't do 360, which isn't a huge deal. But when I was setting up a stable shot, I had to just turn my entire tripod around instead of turning the camera around, which was kind of annoying.• In order to use all the cool features, you got to use their recording app. You can't just use the iPhone app or whatever native camera you have on your phone and then use the device to get the features. The features are within the app, which isn't that big of a deal, but it's kind of annoying.• If you want to use the DJI Microphone with this, it throws off the balance and weight of your phone, and it can be very hard to get an angle that actually works without blocking the movement. I plugged my microphone in to the phone, and then the phone wouldn't turn around; it would get caught because of the microphone. It's weird that it's their microphone; they should make it work better with their gimbal. It's hard, and it kind of throws off the balance of the phone a little bit. I think I found a way by maneuvering the phone that it could spin fairly freely with the microphone plugged in, but it wasn't easy to do and it took maneuvering. So I feel like it should work more seamlessly with their own products or they should have a way to plug the microphone directly into the gimbal so you don't have to worry about that.• Sometimes, if your phone is off balance, you get this little Air notification, and it's pretty annoying. You have to adjust the balance of your phone. That's just kind of the nature of the gimbal having to stabilize your phone, but it is a little bit annoying.But other than that, for $50, I would definitely get this again. If it was $70-80 bucks, then I feel like those little annoyances would make it feel like it's not worth it.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: So I originally purchased the Smooth 5 and I had it on my wishlist for a while but I also upgraded to my iPhone 14 pro. I was sort of skeptical if buying the smooth 5 would not work any well with the new iPhone so I decided to cancel it and get this.BUT LET ME TELL YOU! This thing is an absolute beast for the price.I watched videos on the face tracking and how it stacked up to other Gimbals and honestly this one was #2 when #1 on the Ai face tracking guesser was the insta360 (which was going to be my second option if this one crapped out.)The magnet is SUPER tough and the gimbal itself has some solid weight to it. What I purchased externally were the silicone lights that are OEM to the device but sold separately.This has been my first gimbal and I’m glad it is! I don’t see the other ones doing what this does at this value, I also am using this for small business clips and recordings I can edit on iMovie to stitch some advertising together. I firmly feel like the average person can go from beginner to advanced because of all the features the app has.ALSO, that’s another reason why I purchased this! It came with a tutorial showing you how to set up, to then how to go crazy with your shots! I heard the smooth 5 were some learning curve issues with getting it going. This thing straight off the bat hooked up to the app showed me HOW to use all of it.Notable mentions are the insta360 but also even the OM6 because it comes with its own selfie stick rod and the zoom crank feature.I give this product a solid SOLID 4.9/5The reason being, is because of the lights it could have been bundled with, and of course if you’re looking for a motor that’s gonna lock on to something moving at a high speed this can’t do those things, but if it’s moderate movement it will definitely keep up!I hope this review helps you decide. As I mentioned before. I looked at 6 gimbals around this price point and none of them do the things this can do at this price point for iOS devices at least! I’m not sure about android! But if this is for iPhone? Buy it. Seriously it’s awesome!

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Great phone for the price. I'm a Motorola fan and have been using my two sim Motorola One-the first one they made since 2013. Was getting slow but still a good phone. This model has plenty of built in memory for my needs and the 1tb memory card option is excellent since all the newer phones are deleting that option. It's nice to be able to have that memory card to be able to put in the computer or my android TV box and use the files on other things without having the hassle of trying to connect with other electronics. That being said, this model has an excellent built in mode where it will connect to your computer via usb without any problems or hassle and will transfer and receive files great! Haven't tried it on the android TV box I have yet. It is tough and with a screen protector almost bullet proof. Maybe soft foam nerf bullets. LOL The battery life is most excellent and doesn't seem to heat up very much what few times I've charged it. If you're looking for a great phone that is not in the thousand dollar price range that will do everything it claims to this is the one I'd recommend. Better hurry before they're all gone because the new models don't have the memory card option at all and I think that's a serious mistake on the manufacturers for doing that. I will probably use this phone for the next ten years or longer! Would recommend this phone model to my friends (if I had any) LOL

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Very Good Budget PhoneVery Good Budget Phone
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I received this yesterday and have tried it out for nearly 24 hours now. I will be using this as a back up phone.The pluses.Nice big clear and bright screen.I like the case and the color. It looks and feel quite decent,Good, responsive touchscreen with good colors.Good wifi and bluetooth. On screen keyboard is also easy to use.Large battery, I charged it to 100 % last night and its still at 70%Good sound quality and fairly loud speakers.Negatives.There is some lag but that is in comparison to my “high end” main phone but I consider it to be more than acceptable.The cameras have great colors are appear to be over processed.If this was for use as my main shooter, it  would not be acceptable but for the bargain price, and considering that this is  budget phone, both front and rear cameras will suffice.Not too keen on the side finger print reader, it does work and actually responds quite fast, I don’t care for the location.So as a budget back up phone, there are some negatives but I can live with them all.Not; the first two photos were taken with the rear came at high resolution. The third was taken with the front facing camera. The last two were taken indoors in a restaurant setting on high resolution.I quite like this phone. I had been considering a 5 year old phone for a back up…. It still had really good specs but I was concerned about the battery and how much longer it would work. Also there would not be any security updates on an older phone but this is from 2024 and has already done several updates since I first powered it on, and it is due to be upgraded to Android 14 later this summer. productPageReviews.reviewDescription: The Motorola Moto G Play (2024) is a very budget-friendly smartphone that focuses on the basics rather than high-end performance. It comes with a large 6.5-inch HD+ display, a 50MP main camera, and a strong 5,000mAh battery that easily lasts a full day or more with regular use. It also includes a headphone jack and expandable storage, which are nice extras at this price point.In everyday use, the phone handles texting, browsing, streaming, and social media fairly smoothly thanks to its Snapdragon 680 processor and 4GB of RAM. However, it’s not built for heavy gaming or demanding apps, and performance can feel limited at times.The camera is decent in good lighting but struggles in low light and isn’t very versatile compared to higher-end phones.  The display is also basic, with a 720p resolution that’s fine for casual viewing but not especially sharp.Overall, the Moto G Play (2024) is best suited as a starter phone, backup device, or for users who just need something simple and reliable. It offers solid battery life and basic features at a low price, but it makes clear trade-offs in performance, camera quality, and display sharpness.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Decent Budget Phone, Poor Build Quality/QCDecent Budget Phone, Poor Build Quality/QC
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: As an owner of previous Motorola devices, I'm a little disappointed in this model.  I know its a budget phone, but Motorola's build quality and QC process missed the mark on this model.  I'll start with the positives and then bring up the areas of improvement.PROS-Price:  This is a budget friendly Android phone.  It will not break the bank.-Performance:  Piggybacking off of the fact this phone is a budget model, I will still say that this phone is still speedy *enough* for everyday basic tasks.  This device has a Snapdragon 680 4G SoC (more on the 4G part later).  It also comes with just 4gb of RAM, though you can sort of "expand" virtually it with phone device storage up to a total of 8gb of RAM.  Social Media, Texting, Media Consumption (Music/Videos/etc) & phone calls are all something that can be dealt with easily with the Moto G Play 2024.  Even light gaming would be okay on this device.  I'm not talking Genshin or anything...maybe Pokémon Go or lighter.-Color:  Not gonna lie, this metallic blue looks *awesome* IMO.  I'm a big fan of it.  This phone is also all plastic.  From the rear to the mid and even up to near the front of the phone.  Though I will say the rear has a matte finish and doesn't slip from your hands, and doesn't look too cheap on the whole.-Battery:  5000mah battery in this phone coupled with a lower power SoC means you should get some decent battery life out of it.-Audio Options:  Again, for a budget phone, this thing isn't bad.  Headphone jack, and the down firing speaker sounds pretty good.  Also has Dolby Atmos options.-Expandable Storage:  Now, the base storage of 64gb is a little paltry in today's world of 128gb base models, but you do have the ability to slip in a MicroSD card and expand upon it.  And you'll definitely want to consider that as 64 can fill up pretty quickly.CONS:-Screen:  The screen is a slight letdown.  It is not very bright (500 nits max), and it is an LCD panel as well.  I can give the LCD panel a pass on such a budget model, but that low of a brightness is not fun when you're outdoors.  The refresh rate maxes out at 90hz, which is okay.  The bezels are pretty chunky, especially the bottom/chin of the device.Another saving grace is the glass screen is Corning Gorilla Glass 3, which is nice to have a name-brand glass piece on the front.  There is also no fingerprint reader under the screen on this model (though some people may prefer that).  Instead, it will be on your power button on the right.-Camera:  The camera(s) are a slight letdown to me.  While most Moto devices have 2 cameras, our G Play '24 here only has one.  While the rear may look like it has two camera punchouts, Motorola did a sneaky and slipped the flash into the bottom  punchout.  There is also no OIS (Optical Image Stabilization) which means you need to stay pretty calm and level when taking pictures or videos.  On the up side, the main (only?) rear camera is 50MP, which bins down to about 12.5MP.  Still, the quality isn't exceptional.  But, this is a budget phone.  The front facing camera is only 8MP, and for some reason it does *not* support face unlock, so you're stuck with either typing in your PIN or using the fingerprint reader on the power button.-OS/Updates:  One of the bigger cons on almost any Motorola device is the OS Support and Security Updates.  You'll get one.  One. Major. OS. Update.  This device started on Android 13, and has already had its Android 14 update dropped.  You shouldn't be seeing any other major update now, just security updates for another 2 years.  This is easily surpassed by...anyone really.  Also, the MUX is slightly inferior to the new Hello UI that Motorola has installed on newer Moto devices IMO.  Still, it boasts nice customization options, and things look nice.-Network Compatibility:  This particular device does *not* have a 5G radio installed.  The Moto G Play '24 is limited to 4G LTE networks.  Granted 4G LTE is a mature network with good coverage, you won't be seeing any of the 5G bands on here.  But, I don't see this as a deal-breaker when it comes to the phone.*BIGGEST ISSUE*-Build Quality/QC-My biggest gripe of all here is the build quality.  As seen in the photos, the rear panel does not meet the mid frame properly on the left side of the phone.  There is a slight bump where the mid frame doesn't properly mate to the back panel.  As far as I can tell, there's no easy fix as the back is plastic and is glued in place.  While I *could* return my phone, there is no replacement option.  Instead, I would have to have a full refund issued and re-buy the device.  This is slightly aggravating to me.  So, I'll suck it up and throw a case on it so I don't see the poor build quality.  I know this is a budget device, but this is just sloppy.*BOTTOM LINE/TL;DR*So overall, I can't complain *too* much about the Motorola G Play 2024.  It checks a fair amount of boxes for such a budget phone.  The only *real* concern/issue I have with it is the build quality that occurred on my particular unit.  When it comes to a recommendation, that's a hard one.  There are quite a few compromises made to make this model so inexpensive.  And for a few more dollars you can get something more feature-rich.  I'd say pick this up if you are on a strict budget, or you need a secondary phone to use when you go somewhere you'd worry about damaging your daily driver phone (concert, theme park, etc).

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Good Price but...Phones these days are less about the user and more about being used.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: The unbelievable amount of configuring and disabling to get this intrusive garbage from constantly nagging you is a nightmare. I can't recommend this phone simply because so much of this device is geared toward monetizing you, this is definitely how they make their money back. I was really irritated that the Screensaver app called "Glance" doesn't even have a [X] to close the nag window that kept popping up, I had to use the navigation buttons on the phone to bypass it and then eventually had to find a way to force stop this app. Its just one of the many horribly intrusive programs that's preloaded and impossible to avoid. Just look up how to remove "Glance" Lock Screen. It's unbelievable that not even your lock screen is safe from advertising. GROSSLY PATHETIC. And all the Google settings you have to disable to keep your apps from sending info to google to send you "SUGGESTIONS" What a load of crap. I've used cell phones, just like so many people on the planet without google telling me how to use it. I know what a browser is, I know how to use one to find stuff I want, that's where it ends. NO I DON'T NEED OR WANT YOU GOOGLE. F the F OFF. I try not to even use the G-Play Store, I use F-Droid for Open Source Alternatives. And Android makes sure it's difficult to install unapproved apps, but you can still do it with most free software on F-Droid. Honestly if you want to be free of these intrusions you really have to work hard at it. Another thing I found out about this phone is that there is a tiny IR LED that blinks constantly in the upper right hand of the screen, I have still yet to find out for sure why it's blinking constantly, but from what I have read it might have to do with something related to detecting if the phone is near your face or if the phone is in your pocket, but it blinks ALL THE TIME, look at your Moto G Play 2024 phone with another camera and you will see it blinking too. It's disturbing knowing this device is constantly blinking a light. It's strange because it's not a patterned blink it's like a data signal, so would be interesting to find out if this is actually trying to communicate with other IR devices. No clue but interesting. Aside from my paranoia regarding the light, the phone functions for the most part as intended, as a phone and browser and I use it for multiple apps that seam to operate well on this platform. I just don't see myself owning another Android based phone after this experience, it's just more and more obvious that you have less and less control over what your phone is doing. In my ideal world there would be an open source phone where there is nothing hidden from the user. That's not the case here, so many agreements to click through, who knows what this thing is actually doing half the time. I can be certain it's trying to find ways to analyze my usage so it can predict ways of emptying my wallet. Just a shameful digital world we've entered, it would be nice to see an alternative to all this garbage. I'm already looking into rooting and installing a degoogled mobile OS, but I've done stuff like that before and it's just as much a headache but one with less worry regarding apps spying on you. I needed a new phone and the price was right but that is about as far as the compliments can be extended from me. Phones these days are less about the user and more about being used.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Better Than I Expected for a Refurbished PhoneBetter Than I Expected for a Refurbished Phone
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I picked this up as a backup phone, so I wasn’t expecting it to be perfect. Since it’s an older model, I figured it would probably have some scratches or small dents, but nope... this baby was in way better shape than I expected. The screen looked really good, and I had to actually look closely to find any signs that it had been used. I did put a screen protector and case on it right away because, once I saw the condition it came in, I wanted to keep it that way.Another impressive thing was how easy it was to get everything set up. It powered on with no issues, and transferring my stuff from my old phone was pretty simple. Everything has been running smoothly so far, and I haven’t noticed any overheating, even while setting it up, downloading apps, and using it for a while.And oh man, talk about the screen size. It’s big enough for browsing, watching videos, and reading without making the phone feel huge or awkward to hold. The phone size is actually pretty comfortable, and it still feels durable enough for everyday use.The battery life is not the same as a brand-new iPhone, but that’s expected with a refurbished phone. It still gets me through a normal day, which is really all I needed. For the price and the condition it came in, I’d say it was a solid deal.
